Period tags: Victorian 262, Georgian 87, Edwardian 85, Art Deco 59, Arts and Crafts 18, Art Nouveau 13; counting tagged or explicitly dated pieces about 722 of 1,250 (58%) are dated before 1970 and about 64 (5%) after; the remaining ~37% are undated 'vintage' pieces. Examples: Antique Date 1913 Pink Topaz and Pearl Dress Ring GBP 805.50, Vintage 1960's Deco Emerald and Diamond Cocktail Ring. The about text also mentions secondhand jewellery (borderline: pre-1970 share evidenced at ~58%, rest unknown). No auctions, no contemporary art, no new goods. UK delivery by insured Special Delivery (GBP 8.50 under GBP 250), international FedEx, worldwide shipping.

omissions: UK rate GBP 8.50 applies only to items under GBP 250 (bracket not representable) and international prices are 'usually' GBP 15 or 35, so no rates asserted.
Collection terms not asserted.
No company number published on the pages read.

decision.basis: crystalantiquechandeliers.co.uk is the SellingAntiques-hosted mirror of Crystal Corner Antique Chandeliers (9A Westhorpe Road, Marlow SL7 1LB, crystalcorner@me.com, 07721 518815); its contact page names the dealer's own site https://www.crystal-corner.co.uk/, which was onboarded as the source (same operator, same stock; mirror lists 136 items).

Douglas Fisher Antique Automata Ltd (75 Portobello Road, London W11 2QB; LAPADA, CINOA; sales@douglas-fisher.com) sells genuine antique singing bird boxes and automata (e.g. Karl Griesbaum silver-gilt box circa 1920, Bontems and Bruguier boxes) with detailed itemised descriptions and stock numbers, but no price is shown on the stock list, item pages or the 'buying from us' page; purchase is by telephone or email only. Borderline: antique stock is clearly qualified; only the absence of any published price excludes it.

E. W. Cousins Antiques (27 High Street, Ixworth, Bury St Edmunds IP31 2HJ; est. 1920) is a genuine antique furniture dealer, but its site has only a photo gallery and about/contact pages: no item titles, descriptions or prices (the Furniture page holds only images), so no inspectable stock.

Facet & Fable shows 'Our Creations' (Enlighten, Illuminate and Fable collections), commissions, bridal and gift guides, i.e. newly designed and made jewellery, next to a few antique pieces; the home page still carries placeholder lorem ipsum text and a London Masterpiece 2021 event notice, so the site looks unmaintained. Own new collections are a dedicated new-goods section.

Farnham Antique Carpets sells antique rugs but its carpet menu has dedicated 'Modern' and 'Bespoke' categories and a 'Contemporary' rug section, plus rug underlay, cleaning and restoration services, so newly made rugs are a dedicated shop part.

decorativecollective.com is a multi-seller marketplace (seller profile page of SPINKA & CO, a LAPADA member in Derbyshire); stock of many independent sellers is shown under one platform, so it is not a single dealer storefront.

David Shure Antique Silver (London Silver Vaults, Chancery Lane WC2A 1QS; sales@davidshure.com; 020 7405 0011) is a brochure site with About and Contact only; the 'Shop' link goes to the sister shop I.Franks (ifranks.com), which is another dealer domain handled by another shard. No own catalogue.

Raimu Japanese Antiques Limited t/a David Thatcher Samurai Art (company 06830800; NN12 6DH; LAPADA) sells antique samurai armour (Momoyama kabuto, Maeda clan armour), but the site also runs dedicated shop parts for the proprietor's own new digital-art fine art prints and posters (living-artist work, open and limited editions) and his self-published books through a Shopify store. Dedicated new-goods sections, so NEW_GOODS_MIX. Borderline: the armour core is antique and LAPADA accredited; owner may reconsider if own prints/books are acceptable beside an antique core.

Dinan & Chighine (London, since 1988) sells framed prints and art from the 17th century to the present: categories read on the shop are 17th-19th Century Engravings and Watercolours (48 items, e.g. George Edwards bird engravings 1770), 20th Century Modern Masters (42 items: Miro lithograph 1974, Picasso 1960, Chagall lithographs 1954-61, i.e. editions by post-war masters), a Contemporary Artists category and Furniture and Accessories (about 10 items), with prices in USD. Antique share is below half and a contemporary-artists section exists; editions by modern masters fall under the post-war art exclusion.

DBGEMS (Gray's Antique Market, London; est. 2005; LAPADA; WooCommerce shop) calls itself 'fine antique, vintage and modern jewellery' offering 'authentic antique and vintage jewellery alongside beautifully made contemporary designs'. The shop has a 21st Century period filter and a Wedding Rings collection, product titles such as '18ct yellow gold wedding band' and '1.20ct brilliant cut diamond solitaire engagement ring' give no age, and the store API reports a very large product count that could not be reconciled with the pages. The antique/vintage share and any new-goods share cannot be established from first-party pages; re-check with period counts.

Fable & Windsor (London jewellery company; buyer Nosheen) offers 'antique, vintage and modern jewellery' from the Georgian era to 'edgy, contemporary and defined modern pieces'. The shop page exceeds the fetch limit and no era counts could be read, so the antique/vintage share and any new modern pieces cannot be measured from first-party pages.

Everything dated before about 1950. No auctions, no contemporary art, no new goods; selective restoration is a side service. Open by appointment; contact by telephone.

decision.basis: Danish Homestore (Polsefinger Ltd, company 13114896, 88/94 Derby Road, Nottingham NG1 5FD) sells vintage and mid-century Danish furniture, but the shop also has dedicated sections for newly made goods: 'modern Decorative art' (decorative art items in glass, metal and ceramic), flat woven coloured Danish cord for sale and care and maintenance products. Dedicated new-goods sections, so NEW_GOODS_MIX. Borderline: vintage furniture is the core.

Dorian Caffot de Fawes (Dorian Antiques, Shopify) sells French and Scandinavian Art Deco and mid-century furniture and lighting (107 available of 1,250 listed), but every product price is 0.00 in the public products.json and no price is shown on the shop pages; purchase is by enquiry only.

Denton Antiques (fourth-generation family business, 156 and 166 Kensington Church Street, London W8 4BN; +44 20 7229 5866) sells antique chandeliers, lanterns and lighting from the 18th to early 20th century with itemised stock numbers, but no price appears on the home, collections or item pages and no terms of sale are published; purchase is by enquiry. Borderline: antique stock is qualified; only the missing prices exclude it.

Pinefinders Old Pine Furniture Warehouse (Haddenham, Bucks HP17 8BY; 01844 291231) restores and sells old pine furniture but the shop menu has a dedicated 'Pine Furniture Made To Measure' section and the text says they also make bespoke made-to-measure pine furniture 'made from new or reclaimed pine': dedicated new-goods part. Borderline: old pine is the core; no email address published.

Clive Payne (Unit 11, Langston Priory Workshops, Kingham OX7 6UP; BAFRA and LAPADA member) is mainly an antique furniture restoration business; the Antiques section (Winson Antiques, Mason's Ironstone China, a Regency music stand) shows a small archive-style gallery with no prices and no purchase option.

Charlotte Fine Jewellery (PrestaShop-style shop) describes a 30-year London dealer specialising in period and antique gem-set jewellery from about 1750 to the late 20th century, with signed Cartier, Van Cleef and Arpels, Bulgari and Tiffany pieces (Edwardian Ruby Heart Pendant GBP 6,500 among them). The contact page shows the webmaster address miles@gv-media.com rather than a dealer address, service@charlottefinejewellery.com appears elsewhere, no street address, company name or company number is published and the era mix of the signed pieces is not stated. Operator identity and antique share cannot be established; recheck for an imprint.

Cheshire Antiques Consultant LTD (incorporated 22 April 2024, registered office Covent Garden; Shopify; 486 products, 430 available) sells British and European paintings and bronzes, mostly described as 19th/20th century. Tags show 20th century 232, 19th century 185, 21st century 31 and contemporary 15; sampled 21st-century items are living-artist works painted 2005-2022 (about 6-9% of stock, above the trivial share) and many titles are 'After ...', 'in the manner of' or 'style' copies whose age is not stated. Whether the modern copies and contemporary works stay below the new-goods and contemporary-art limits cannot be settled from the pages; recheck with a full per-item review.

Guest & Gray (58 Davies Street, Gray's Antiques Market, London W1K 5LP; mobile +44 7968 719496; showroom by appointment) is a strong candidate: the catalogue counts 811 Chinese, 143 Japanese/Islamic/Indian, 365 European and 128 other objects (one contemporary object) of antique ceramics. The fetcher only sees category counts, not object lists, prices or item pages (they load dynamically), no email address is published (message form only) and no legal operator is named. Render the catalogue with a headless browser to confirm prices and the operator before onboarding.

The Clock Clinic (Putney, London SW15 1EU; time@clockclinic.co.uk; 020 8788 1407; 'registered in England and Wales', 50 years of repairs) sells antique and vintage clocks, but the shop also lists 'Gifts for Watch Lovers' and a general 'Watches For Sale - Stylish and Elegant' category; product lists load dynamically so the antique share and any new gifts or modern watches could not be measured. Recheck by rendering the shop.

David Brower Antiques (Kensington Church Street, London; est. 1964; LAPADA) sells 19th-century European and Oriental antiques (Meissen, KPM, sculpture, Japanese and Chinese porcelain). The legacy site shows category pages with price bands (A under GBP 1,000 to F price on application) and no per-item prices, and the home page still promotes a June lockdown exhibition (2020), so current stock and activity are unconfirmed.

Home page of Gallery Yacou (London, family carpet business) states it specialises in 'antique, decorative and contemporary carpets' and its collection navigation has dedicated 'Recreations' and 'Contemporary' sections alongside antique Persian carpets (featured: Kirman c.1890-1910). Dedicated new-goods sections (recreations = newly made carpets, contemporary carpets) breach the no vintage/new mix rule. Gatsby Jewellery (Theydon Bois, Essex; Shopify, 454 products in products.json) sells mostly antique/vintage rings (about 96% of titles carry Victorian to 1970s periods; circa-dating histogram 1850-1980) but its navigation has a dedicated 'Bespoke Gatsby Bands' / 'The Gatsby Collection' section of newly made-to-order wedding bands (e.g. 'Eliza', 'Grace', 'Wendy', 'Vera': custom crafted in platinum/gold, 'Fully bespoke'), a dedicated new-goods part of the shop under the 2026-11-26 no vintage/new mix rule. No auction activity seen.

Gentle Rattle of China (Willa Latham, Wix site) sells antique English porcelain (Spode, Minton, Derby, Worcester, circa 1760-1835, priced in GBP, contact page says London, United Kingdom, email only). Home page banner states 'We have moved! We are in the process of getting set up in our new location in France ... we will let you know when we are ready to re-open the online shopping functions'; orders are by emailed quote and invoice meanwhile. Home country (GB vs FR), operating base and the online catalogue's activity are therefore unresolved; defer rather than guess. Re-check when the shop re-opens; may belong to the FR shard if the imprint moves to France.

Alastair Gibson Antiques: the home page is a single image-map graphic (page text is only the name) with links to a BADA dealer profile, an email address, social profiles and alastairgibsonauctions.com, the proprietor's separate auction house for Asian art (last auction 7 November 2026). No product listings, prices, imprint, phone or address are published on gibsonantiques.com, so there is no inspectable stock, operator or location to qualify; the https variant fails certificate verification. The proprietor also runs an auction business.

Goodwins (Goodwin Antiques Ltd vendor, Edinburgh, two retail showrooms on Queensferry Street and Rose Street, Shopify, 790 products in products.json) is a fourth-generation retail jeweller and silver dealer that also offers jewellery and watch repairs. Measured by title: only about 46% of products carry an antique/vintage/period marker (Victorian, Edwardian, Art Deco, Georgian, antique, vintage, circa, pre-1970 dates); the other 429 of 790 are undated 9ct/18ct/platinum modern-style jewellery (e.g. Vera Wang, brilliant-cut diamond stud earrings, 'modern charm' descriptions). Not predominantly antique or vintage (policy C, more than half required). No auction activity seen.

Hancocks London (62 St James's Street, Magento shop, est. 1849) sells antique and vintage jewellery but its shop also has a dedicated 'Jewels by Hancocks' contemporary collection ('unique handcrafted jewellery designed in house and created by our talented craftsmen', about 296 items in the price filter), wedding/engagement/bridal bands, Limited Edition Replica Victoria Cross and 'GRIMA for Hancocks' lines. Dedicated new-goods sections make it a vintage/new mix under the 2026-11-26 rule. No auction activity checked beyond the shop.

The lead is a dealer profile page on graysantiques.com, the website of Grays Antiques, a multi-dealer antiques centre/marketplace (the page lists 'Home | Dealers | Anthea AG Antiques Ltd.', Stand No. 155, a filter over several dealers' stock, contact via info@graysantiques.com). It is not the dealer's own shop. The dealer (Anthea AG Antiques Ltd., fine jewellery circa 1840-1990s, LAPADA and BADA member) has no own site established; queued as an own-domain lead only.

go.berganza.com is a Bitly branded short domain (landing page 'branded short domains powered by Bitly') used for tracked links such as the LAPADA referral; it is not a shop. The dealer is Berganza Ltd at www.berganza.com, handled in this shard under that domain.

Horton London (David Horton, LAPADA, stand 322 Grays Antiques Market; PH9 site) sells a mix: antique and vintage jewellery and 19th/20th century art, but the shop also lists made-to-order new pieces (platinum diamond half eternity and engagement rings 'To Order from', GIA-certified modern diamond rings) and a Studio Pottery section of post-1970 work including living artists (e.g. Edmund de Waal cargo jar 1998, Helen Felcey 2009, Alan Wallwork 1980s-1990s, Robin Welch 1988). New made-to-order goods plus a large post-1970 studio pottery category mean the stock is not predominantly antique or vintage and is a vintage/new mix (2026-11-26 rules). No auction activity seen.

Heming (London jeweller, Magento-style shop with account/privacy-center routes) navigation lists mainly its own new collections: Christian Bauer Collection, Heming Collections (Diamond, Cascade, Kaleidoscope, Renaissance, Zodiac, Diamond Initials, Pearl), engagement rings '1745 Collection', 'Radiance Collection', classic and diamond wedding/eternity rings, with only a single 'Vintage Collection' entry. A new-goods jewellery retailer, not an antiques dealer; the vintage section is a minor part. No auction activity checked.

Thomas Heneage Art Books (42 Duke Street St James's, London; ABA/ILAB/LAPADA member) states its core business is books for the art market: catalogues raisonnes, monographs and international exhibition catalogues, 'irrespective of its being new or second hand', plus new-title information, library-building, valuation and bookbinding services; antiquarian books and objects of fine art are mentioned as an extra. The stock is predominantly modern reference books (new and used), not majority antique/vintage (policy C). Triage flagged auction; not needed for the decision.

History Coins (IONOS MyWebsite, ancient Greek/Roman, hammered and milled coins, antiquities, fossils, 'Gifts' section) publishes a contact form and the email reply@historycoins.co.uk but deliberately no telephone number, no postal address and no operator name: the legal notice says 'Our name:' followed only by numismatic qualifications and that contact details are given only to bona fide customers. The home page also carries a notice 'FOR SALE PRICES - SOON TO BE REMOVED', so the shop's continued activity is uncertain. Without a legal operator and a location the row cannot be built faithfully; re-check later (a coin dealer's antique scope itself is not contested).

Hunt Vintage (WooCommerce) describes itself as a platform that 'brings together a trusted community of vetted professional sellers offering vintage furniture, antiques, iconic fashion, art, and jewellery', has a 'become a seller' page and shows 'pieces from our hottest vintage and antique boutiques'. A multi-seller marketplace, not one dealer's own stock. The lead URL was a sold-out sideboard product page.

J. McCarthy Ltd (Mayfair antique and fine jeweller, WooCommerce, 230 products in the store API): 152 of 230 product titles (66%) carry no antique/vintage/period marker and are plain modern or estate pieces such as '18ct Gold Diamond Cluster Ring', 'Platinum Diamond Five Stone Ring', 'Tiffany & Co. Sterling Silver Heart Tag Necklace', '9ct Gold Mariner Link Bracelet'; only about 34% are marked antique, vintage, Edwardian, Art Deco etc. The business also advertises repairs, valuations and bespoke jewellery. Not predominantly antique or vintage (policy C), so not onboarded.

Jenna Burlingham Gallery (Artlogic site, Hampshire-Berkshire border) describes itself as 'A Modern British and Contemporary Art Gallery' showing '20th Century and Contemporary British paintings, prints, sculpture and ceramics' with artists, exhibitions and a cart. Stock is modern and contemporary art by 20th-century and living artists, not predominantly pre-1945 (policy 2026-11-24/26). No auction check needed.

John Adams Fine Art (London, Artlogic site) is titled '20th Century Contemporary Art for Sale' and sells School of Paris and Modern British painters; its artist list (Ambrogiani, Cavailles, de Botton, Dyf, Grau Sala, Papart, Schneider, Mendjisky, Frederick Gore, Peter Kelly, Claude Grosperrin and others) is dominated by artists active mainly after 1945, with works dated e.g. 1965 (Racoff, Place des Vosges), and includes living or recently active artists. Not predominantly pre-1945, so excluded under the 2026-11-26 modern/post-war art rule.

Joanna Booth (Shopify, 117 products: old master drawings, early wood carvings, textiles/tapestries, sculpture, circa 1450-1800, GBP prices) publishes no telephone number, no email address and no postal address on its home, About or Contact page (enquiry form only; About mentions viewing by appointment at an apartment and storage in Chelsea and a mill on the Welsh borders, closed Kings Road shop in 2007). No operator name or legal form is published either. Stock qualifies on its face, but a Party cannot be built faithfully without published contact data; re-check later.

Gallery B.R (Cotswolds, Artlogic site) describes itself on its gallery page as 'a contemporary gallery with an established presence in the UK' (founders Pep and Cuca, 25 years in 20th-century design and antiques); the menu is Art (represented artists), Design, Antiques and Exhibitions. The gallery programme is contemporary art and design with antiques as one of three strands, so the stock is not predominantly antique/vintage and the business is a contemporary-art gallery under the 2026-11-24 policy.

Japanese Gallery Kensington Limited (company 10841426, 66E Kensington Church Street, London W8 4BY) sells antique ukiyo-e prints, swords, lacquer and ceramics from a fixed-price catalogue, but the main navigation also has a dedicated 'Anime & Manga Store' selling 'Original' and vintage anime posters and cels of 1990s-2020s series (Demon Slayer, Naruto, Spirited Away, Pokemon, Dragon Ball) at about GBP 110-700: a post-1970 modern collectibles shop part, outside the antique/vintage scope and a vintage/modern mix under the 2026-11-26 rules. AUCTION SIDE ACTIVITY (noted for the owner): the gallery also runs the separate JG Auction department/site (jgauction.com) with consignment auctions. Catalogue pages returned HTTP 403, so section sizes could not be measured.

James Jewels (Unit 152, Grays Antiques Centre, 58 Davies Street, Mayfair; Shopify, 77 products) sells antique and vintage jewellery, but the storefront is not in a state to qualify: products.json contains a 'testtest' product and about half of the items carry a placeholder price of GBP 1.37 or 'POA'; the visible pages show no telephone or email (the email jamesofmayfair@hotmail.com and phone 020 7409 1874 appear only in page meta descriptions); no legal operator is named. Stock looks antique/vintage but facts and prices are unreliable; re-check when the catalogue is complete.

decision.basis: J.W.B Coins & Collectables (Shopify, more than 3,000 products, family business started on eBay in 2007) sells mostly pre-1970 coins (about 87% of the year-dated titles sampled), banknotes, tokens and antique silver, but the shop also has a dedicated Gifts section with 'beautifully handcrafted greetings cards' (Christmas Greetings Cards, Greetings Card Hub), 'Stocking Fillers & Small Gifts', assembled mounted and framed Birth Year Coin Sets, a 'modern-commemorative-coins-for-sale' collection, proof sets and gift cards. Dedicated new-goods and gift sections, so excluded as a vintage/new mix; a general collectables seller (stamps, postcards, jewellery, militaria, art, memorabilia) rather than a specialist dealer.

The Old Map Company (Cornwall workshop, WooCommerce shop, 778 products): the map catalogue consists of newly printed fine art reproductions of old maps (home page: 'We make fine art prints of old maps, right here in our Cornwall workshop'; product text: 'Reproduced from a particularly attractive coloured edition ... a certified FINE ART PRINT', GBP 35.55 to 59.95), plus new reproduction railway station clocks ('Windsor & Eaton Reproduction Railway Station Clock', 'Our Clocks' 211 and 'Railway Clocks' 151 listings). Policy: shops selling new prints, reproductions or decorative wall art are out; no original antique stock.

Raccoon Deals is an affiliate content/deal-aggregator site (buying guides, 'Verified sellers with high ratings, Secure payment through eBay', Amazon deal roundups); the product pages are eBay/Amazon listings of third-party sellers across every category (fashion, electronics, automotive, antiques ...). No own stock, no operator imprint: marketplace-only/affiliate content, not an antiques dealer.

Smithers of Stamford (redirects to smithers.co) is a general furniture and home-decor retailer: shop-by-style ranges 'Luxe Creations', 'Prestige Editions', Reclaimed Wood, Industrial, Rattan, Neon Signs, Bespoke, Wallpaper, Robots, Gifts, Vases, with 'Black Friday Sales' and pay-later finance; 'Antique Furniture' is only one style among many new/upcycled ranges. Newly made goods are far beyond the 5 percent tolerance.

Studio Ham (Shopify, 1,072 products) is a design studio selling its own new art, framed prints/flags, 'Folky' made furniture, bathroom vanities, cushions, wallpaper, gifting and merch alongside 44 'Antiques' and 31 'Antique Furniture' items; the Art category (477) is contemporary work (e.g. 'Bozeman Boys, Montana 1990' Painting). New goods far exceed the 5 percent tolerance and the antique share is well below half.

Saddington's Jewellery (WooCommerce, 222 products; Tom Saddington Ltd, registered address 20a High Street, Glastonbury BA6 9DU; stand at Gray's Antique Market W1K 5LP): describes 'Georgian, Victorian, Edwardian, Art Deco, Art Nouveau, Vintage and contemporary jewellery'. Only about 102 of 222 titles (46 percent) are explicitly antique/pre-1970; about 30 titles are 1970s onward, 'Contemporary', 'Millennium' or modern signed pieces (Kutchinsky 1970s, Tiffany Paloma Picasso, Patrick Mavros, Georg Jensen) and the rest are undated 'Vintage' or plain titles, so a majority of antique or vintage (pre-1970) goods cannot be shown. Borderline; recheck with item descriptions or a dated stock breakdown.

Patrick Sandberg Antiques (150-152 Kensington Church Street, London W8 4BN, +44 207 229 0373, info@sandbergantiques.com, VAT 08758836; BADA/LAPADA; Wix site): Georgian and Regency furniture is shown as featured items with stock numbers (e.g. 'Antique pair of Regency period rosewood cabinets') and category/period galleries, but no price, price-on-application marker or purchase path could be read in the cached or rendered pages (items are Wix gallery images) and no item detail page was reachable. Stock itself would qualify; identity and item-level evidence are incomplete.

Priory Fine Art Limited (company 07294226, VAT 293684065, Maidstone Cottage, The Close, Averham NG23 5RP; Shopify): of 221 products only 5 are currently available: one painting (Aurel Naray 1883-1948, GBP 3,750), two listings of antique picture-framing moulds, a 'New Frames Made to Order' product and a frame restoration service; all other products are an archive of sold works, including living-era artists (Ken Howard, Fred Cuming) and used modern Rolex watches (a 'Watches For Sale' collection). Current qualified stock is too thin to judge, and the new-frames and modern-watch lines would need an owner check.

No business location can be asserted.

Whether the own fixed-price shop or the eBay auction channel is the main business cannot be established from the site; the terms of service are a generic US-style template whose shipping table (free UK, GBP 20 Europe) contradicts the '+ postage' shop display. AUCTION SIDE ACTIVITY versus auction-led operation needs a decision.

First-party location and stock evidence are incomplete.

The 'Antique & Reclaimed' range is only one collection of a mainly new-goods catalogue sold to the hospitality trade. No auctions seen. Not predominantly antique or vintage.

Home page states 'This website is no longer active' and only points to other third-party sites (Antiques Boutique marketplace, a web-design service, a militaria marketplace, an eCommerce site builder). No stock, no operator or contact details.

Muse. Tomasso (Leeds and London, founded 1993, TEFAF exhibitor, MasterArt platform) deals in European sculpture, master paintings and ancient art, which would qualify as stock, but the website shows no prices anywhere: every inventory item (e.g. Gerard David 'The Lamentation', Luigi Valadier ormolu-mounted porphyry urns, Foggini bronzes) has only an 'Enquire' button and phone number, there is no cart, no shop terms and no delivery terms. No auctions seen. Excluded because there is no inspectable priced catalogue.

Town House, Spitalfields is described by its own text as a gallery, shop and coffee shop that has changed from an antique shop to one selling 'a range of ceramics, both new and old, books, art and interesting antiques when I find them', with a cafe selling cakes and regular exhibitions by contemporary artists (Doreen Fletcher, Chris Thompson, Eleanor Crow, Nicholas Borden). New ceramics, contemporary exhibitions and a coffee shop; antiques are incidental and there is no online catalogue of antique stock.

Carlton Clocks (Somerset, WordPress site with priced clocks) sells antique clocks but its own text says it stocks 'a large range of antique clocks and new clocks', the shop has a dedicated 'Modern Clocks' category (newly made clocks by Erwin Sattler, Kieninger, Matthew Norman and Devon Clocks, e.g. Erwin Sattler Striking Regulator GBP 7,580, with a sale on them) and an 'Electric Clock Parts' category of newly manufactured parts (Brillie battery holder GBP 98). A dedicated new-goods section is a NEW_GOODS_MIX. No auctions seen.

Vagabond Antiques (Market Square, Petworth; founder Joe Chaffer, LAPADA member; Artlogic site) offers fine European antiques (18th and 19th century sculpture, Venetian candlesticks, marble tables, a Coade figure), which would qualify as stock, but none of the 30 collection pages shows a price (every page has an empty price widget and an 'Enquire' button; 7 of them checked in detail), so there is no inspectable priced catalogue. Delivery and showroom terms exist but cannot compensate. No auctions seen.

geography.addressText: Time Militaria, 14 High Street, Hythe, Kent, CT21 5AT, United Kingdom

qualification.basis: Time Militaria, 14 High Street, Hythe, Kent: militaria dealer with a showroom open Fridays and Saturdays 10am-4pm and by appointment, selling original period militaria in its own shop with priced items (e.g. WW2 German Eastern Territory button GBP 20). Catalogue sections: World War I (about 380 listed items), World War II (about 1,230), Post World War II (about 150) and Police Collectables (about 530, historical police badges such as Victorian constabulary buckles and helmet plates). The terms state items are of original period manufacture unless stated otherwise, so roughly 70 percent or more of the stock is WW1 or WW2 and the police section is largely older badges. Historical militaria and Third Reich items are acceptable under the owner policy. Auction check: no auctions. New-goods check: no reproductions seen. Contemporary-art check: none. No legal entity or proprietor name is published; the trading name is used as operator.

shipping: UK posting is free only under a 'current promotion' and overseas postage is at the prevailing air mail rate; only the explicit worldwide export scheme is asserted, no rates; collection not stated

Minor non-antique parts: a Hire category (about 43 hire-service listings), natural history fossils and minerals (about 68) and a handful of contemporary pieces (a few framed prints, a laser-cut fire basket, some contemporary stained glass); together far below half and the genuinely new goods about 1 percent. Auction check: no auctions; the site buys salvage. Contemporary-art check: only a few items, not a stock focus.

value.label: Unique Antiques by Emma Jade, Ipswich

geography.addressText: Main Road, Ipswich, Suffolk, United Kingdom

qualification.basis: Unique Antiques by Emma Jade (Ipswich, Suffolk): independent dealer with a priced online shop of about 1,360 listed items, almost all titled antique Victorian, Edwardian, Regency, Georgian or 19th century pieces, e.g. antique Victorian walnut inlaid credenza, a set of eight antique Regency mahogany bar back dining chairs, Doulton Lambeth jardinieres, Royal Doulton vases, Victorian spelter figures GBP 465, Staffordshire lions GBP 675, Victorian papier-mache collectors cabinet GBP 1,595; clock garnitures and longcase clocks (clock purchases page). Estimated over 95 percent antique. Contact page gives only 'Main Road, Suffolk, Ipswich' with no postcode and no showroom or opening-hours claim, so only a published business address is recorded. Operator is the trading name only (no company or proprietor named in the terms). Auction check: none. New-goods check: none. Contemporary-art check: none.

omissions: shipping: UK delivery is included on the majority of items but furniture and larger items need a quote, so no free-delivery or rate claim is asserted; only that UK delivery and worldwide shipping are offered
legal entity or proprietor not published; postcode and street number not published; no collection statement

decision.basis: Valerie Main Ltd (Carlisle, Cumbria; sellingantiques.co.uk platform; priced catalogue of 1,143 listed items) specialises in Royal Worcester, Coalport, Royal Crown Derby and Hadleys Worcester porcelain. The largest category, 'Royal Worcester Fruit Painted Items Post 1940', holds 614 of 1,143 listings (about 54 percent); its items are by painters such as T Nutt, James Skerrett, John Smith, K Mason, D Winter and P English, many of whom worked into the 1970s-1990s, and the item pages give no dates. Whether more than half of the stock is pre-1970 cannot be established from the first-party pages (a pre-1940 category, floral, bird and animal categories also exist), so it is not onboarded and not excluded. Re-check with item dates or the owner decision. Operator is a limited company by name (Valerie Main Ltd) but no company number or street address is published (Carlisle only). No auctions seen.

Van Den Bosch (Jan and Carole Van Den Bosch, stall at Grays Antique Market, 58 Davies Street, Mayfair, shop open Wednesdays and by appointment) specialises in Arts and Crafts, Art Nouveau and Jugendstil silver and jewellery, which would qualify as stock, but the hand-built static site (last updated 28 February 2022) is a photo gallery with descriptions and hallmarks and no prices at all ('if you require information or prices about any item do not hesitate to contact us'), no cart and no delivery terms. Operator is a market stall; no inspectable priced catalogue.

Howard Walwyn Fine Antique Clocks (123 Kensington Church Street, London W8 7LP, WooCommerce catalogue of about 555 pieces such as a Joseph Knibb table clock and a John Poole marine chronometer) deals in genuine antique clocks, but every product has price 0, is not purchasable ('Read more') and carries only 'Make an enquiry' - no prices anywhere on the site and no delivery terms. No inspectable priced catalogue. No auctions seen.

Watling Reclamation Yard (near Towcester, Northamptonshire; WooCommerce) sells building materials and garden goods including dedicated new-goods categories: 'Bricks: Reclaimed & New', 'Contemporary & New Garden Features', 'New Statuary & Ornamental', 'New Stone Balls & Plinths', fountains, fire bowls, compost bark and mulch, 'Weather It Garden Products'. A builders' merchant and reclamation yard with dedicated new goods, not an antiques dealer.

Wimpole Antiques (Lynn Lindsay, stall at Grays Antique Market, 58 Davies Street, London; LAPADA and BADA member) shows wearable period jewellery 1790-1970 on a static hand-built site (bracelets, brooches, cufflinks, earrings, pendants, rings pages with 'click images for more information') with no prices, no cart and no delivery terms. Photos only; no inspectable priced catalogue.

Winsor Birch is a London art gallery whose programme is exhibitions of living artists (Jack Coulter 'With Every Light and With Every Song' July 2026, 'CLASH LIVE x Jack Coulter', Hector McDonnell 'Istanbul's Light') plus fair participation (British Art Fair, LAPADA Fair Berkeley Square); the stock is contemporary art, not antiques. No inspectable antique stock.

Witney Antiques (Rebecca Scott, 100 Corn Street, Witney, Oxfordshire; BADA, CADA and LAPADA member, founded 1963) specialises in early English samplers, needlework and 17th to early 19th century furniture, which would qualify as stock, but the website's CGI stock pages are a selective gallery ('only a small selection of our stock is on the web site') with no prices on the list or item pages, no cart and no delivery terms; the site notes email problems and a closure until 2 February 2027. No inspectable priced catalogue.

qualification.basis: Vintage Clocks (owner James, a horologist; British Watch and Clock Makers Guild and British Horological Institute member), 4 Bath Road, Stonehouse, Gloucestershire: shop and workshop with opening hours, WooCommerce shop of about 740 priced clocks and watches, almost all antique or vintage (French carriage and mantel clocks c.1880-1900, Victorian fusee bracket clocks, Georgian longcase clocks, Art Deco mantel clocks c.1930, American New Haven clocks c.1880), e.g. Antique French solid ormolu mantel clock c.1880 GBP 950; only about 10 of 739 listings carry a 1970-1985 date (ca1970 wall clocks), under 2 percent. AUCTION SIDE ACTIVITY: the owner is consultant horologist for the third-party John Rolfe Auctions in Tetbury and the shipping page offers to pick, pack and ship buyers' winning lots there; no auctions of its own and the shop sells own stock at fixed prices. Clock repair, servicing and restoration are a separate service. New-goods check: none. Contemporary-art check: none. No legal entity or surname is published; the trading name is used as operator.

omissions: shipping: a distance-based hand-delivery charge (GBP 60 under 40 miles) and packing service (GBP 25) are not asserted as rates; only worldwide shipping is asserted; no collection statement
legal entity, proprietor surname and company number not published

qualification.basis: Wessex Coins, UK numismatic dealers (BNTA, IAPN and ANA member) with a priced online shop of ancient Greek and Roman coins, British hammered and early milled coins, commemorative medals, shipwreck and treasure coins and world coins, e.g. an Edward III gold noble treaty period GBP 7,995, a Charles I 1643 Declaration silver half pound GBP 8,950, Attica Athens silver tetradrachms GBP 1,250-3,800 (62 premier items alone). Stock is ancient, medieval and early modern numismatic material, i.e. antique collectables. Contact page gives a PO box and a mobile number only; the email address is not published (enquiry form) so only the phone is asserted and the PO box is recorded as a correspondence address with no showroom claim. Operator is the trading name only ('Wessex Coins'). Auction check: none. New-goods check: none. Contemporary-art check: none.

email: not published, only an enquiry form; legal entity not published
shipping: the UK fee is asserted as a lower bound only because the GBP 10 and GBP 12 bands depend on order value; international destinations unspecified

decision.basis: Woodham-Smith Ltd (Thomas Woodham-Smith, antique dealer and art adviser, founder of the Treasure House Fair) shows about 300 antiques in categories (87 furniture pre-1900, 58 lighting, 69 objects, 23 pictures) plus a '20th and 21st century furniture' category of 24 items, but every listed item carries a placeholder price of GBP 0.00 (checked on the 30 furniture listings), there is no cart and no delivery terms; the about page says he also deals privately. No inspectable priced catalogue. No auctions seen.

Worcester Antiques Ltd (online-only family business in Worcestershire, own stock, priced items, UK and worldwide insured shipping, no shop premises) describes its stock as 'Antiques & 20th Century Collectables': 18th and 19th century antiques and Asian pieces alongside many modern collectables: six Lorna Bailey pottery items (living designer), Royal Crown Derby limited-edition paperweights (Cheryl Hallam), a Moorcroft ginger jar, Beswick and Sylvac animals, Royal Worcester Doughty figures and collectable series pieces, sculpture by Witold Gracjan Kawalec, and 'original art and notable artist limited edition signed prints'. Of about 56 item pages found in the sitemap a large part (roughly a third or more) is post-1970 or modern, so a majority of pre-1970 stock cannot be established and a new-goods or modern-art mix cannot be ruled out. Not onboarded, not excluded; re-check with the owner's guidance on 20th century collectables. No auctions seen.

Zebrak London Ltd (Mayfair, by appointment only, est. 1985) specialises in antique and signed vintage jewellery (Cartier, Van Cleef and Arpels, Boucheron) but the website is a single brochure page (about and enquiries form) with no catalogue, no prices, no stock listing, no address and no phone number; only info@zebrak.com is published. Nothing inspectable to onboard.

Art and Horse Racing Gallery (Newmarket, established 2023) is a fine art gallery representing about 50 regional, national and international living artists (roster of painters and sculptors with solo exhibitions, advent exhibition and art fairs); a '19th and 20th Century Artwork' section exists but the stock is predominantly the work of contemporary artists. No auctions seen.

The domain redirects to chicagoartmagazine.com, which serves an Indonesian online-slot spam page ('Slot Gacor Online ... Maxwin') copied from a Samsung shop template; no dealer, antiques or contact details. Hijacked or spam domain, not a business.

ArtHistorical Ltd (London; Squarespace site) deals in European sculpture and works of art of museum quality (e.g. an attributed Peter Scheemakers marble bust of Frederick, Prince of Wales circa 1740-50), which would qualify as stock, but the current inventory is only about five works (two marked Sold), each with a placeholder price of GBP 0.00 and no cart terms, no delivery terms and no prices. No inspectable priced catalogue. No auctions seen.

Ashton Rare Books (30 Glebe Road, Market Harborough) describes itself as 'Modern First Editions' with subject sections for the Booker Prize, Philip Pullman, Seamus Heaney, children's fiction, cookery and signed titles; the front-page sample of recent additions is dated 1922, 1952, 1958, 1970 and 1980. Modern first editions and used modern books do not meet the more-than-half pre-1970 antique or vintage rule (pre-1970 share not shown to exceed half; sections devoted to living or recent authors). No auctions seen.

baumkotter.com serves a free parking page of 123 Reg ('is parked free, courtesy of 123 Reg') with advertising links; no business, contact details or stock are visible. No closure notice, so only the domain state is recorded.

value.label: Young and Son gallery, 12 Church Street, London

qualification.basis: Young and Son (Portobello Fine Art Ltd trading as Young and Son, registered in England and Wales 3218924; footer reads 12 Church Street, London NW8 8EP), a gallery in the Church Street antiques street near Alfies Antique Market, selling antiques and fine art with prices through a Shopify shop of about 19 items, e.g. fine Victorian mahogany writing desk GBP 1,200, Napoleon III mahogany mirror c.1870-1900 GBP 2,400, Gloucestershire stone medieval knight sculpture GBP 7,500, portrait attributed to Thomas Hudson GBP 18,000, Burne-Jones 1905 collotype GBP 370, two Sir William Russell Flint works (1880-1969), vintage Piaget watch. About 15 of the 19 listings are antique or vintage; the rest are a 1970s wall clock, a 1982 poster and two Adler jewellery items. A small catalogue is not a reason to exclude. The about page also offers valuations. Auction check: none. New-goods check: none seen. Contemporary-art check: none.

omissions: shipping: the about page only says it has contacts to arrange shipping quotes locally and worldwide; no destinations or terms asserted
no explicit statement of collection or opening hours

decision.basis: Burlington (owner Angela Hardy, London, BADA/LAPADA, viewing by appointment) shows 78 listed 19th/20th-century British and European oil paintings (Leader, Herring, Olsson, de Breanski, Galien-Laloue) but the catalogue gives only a price category per work ('A: Under GBP 5,000' ... 'G: Over GBP 50,000') and many are marked SOLD, so there is no inspectable item price. The About page also says it represents 'a number of leading contemporary and modern artists' (about 11 of the 78 listed works are by living painters such as Paul Gribble b.1938, Carl Whitfield b.1958). No postal address (only 'Burlington, London, by appointment only'), no company or VAT details, no delivery terms (BADA on-premises sales conditions only). Auction check: none; stock otherwise qualifies as antique art.

Camburn Fine Art sells paintings by a handful of living contemporary artists (artists page: Alan Halliday, Jo Minoprio, Giampiero Nanni, Daniel Texier) in categories such as opera/ballet/theatre, landscapes of Morocco, South of France, Venice carnival, with prices GBP 459-17,000 (e.g. 'The Magic Flute' GBP 12,500, 'Blue Nude' GBP 8,500). No antique or historic stock; the contact number on the site is a French (+33) number, so the home country is also unclear.

Carol Tresor (London and Montevideo) offers natural crystals and amethyst mineral formations, sourced from mines and sold as sculptural decor ('hand crafted crystals, amethysts'; exhibitions and catalogues). Natural mineral specimens are not antiques or vintage goods and there is no antique/vintage stock.

Castlegate House Art Gallery, Cumbria, describes itself as a '20th Century British and Contemporary Art Gallery'. The artist roster mixes 20th-century and post-war painters and potters (Blackadder, Gillies, Kyffin Williams, Rie/Coper) with living contemporary artists (e.g. Ceri Allen, Ray Atkins, 'internationally lauded living' painters) and a 'Modern Alternatives, Mid-Century' section. Predominantly post-war and contemporary art, not predominantly pre-1945.

David Simon Contemporary, Castle Cary (est. 2006): British painting, original prints, sculpture and ceramics 'by both established and emerging artists'; artist list is living contemporary artists (Deborah Jackson, Dion Salvador Lloyd, Alice Corbett, Mike Service ...) plus editions of Chagall, Dali, Le Corbusier, Matisse, Picasso, and an 'Artworks under GBP 1000' section. Contemporary art gallery.

Didier Ltd (company 07540064, 66b Kensington Church Street, London W8 4BY) deals in 'artistic jewels designed by leading Modern Masters and designers from the second half of the 20th century' (Calder, Man Ray, Fontana, Pol Bury 1974, Pomodoro; catalogues on Pop Art jewellery, jewellery by contemporary painters and sculptors, produced often in small limited editions). Predominantly post-war artists' jewellery and editions, not predominantly pre-1945 or pre-1970.

C.J. & A.J. Dixon Ltd (Companies House 01365683, 23 Prospect Street, Bridlington; trading as Dixons Medals) sells genuine British orders, decorations and campaign medals (about 1,000 of 1,321 WooCommerce products, e.g. Waterloo Medal 1815) but the shop also carries a dedicated 'Books' section of 207 items (about 140 current reference titles and annual publications such as 'Medal Yearbook 2027', 'Soldiers died in the Great War' volumes and 'New Hard Back Book', next to second-hand books), an 'Accessories' section of newly made King Charles III Coronation medal ribbons, replacement rings, 'copy' medals and badges, gift vouchers and Dixon's Gazette subscriptions. New goods are about 12 percent of the catalogue plus dedicated new-goods sections, well above the trivial share. Auction check: only an agent bidding service for clients (5 percent fee), no own auctions.

Fairhead Fine Art: 'Original prints and drawings by Modern Masters' - post-war and living artists (George Condo, Karel Appel, Maria Helena Vieira da Silva, an 'Untitled (Miles Davis series)' print, 1988 International Volunteer Day print). Editions and multiples by post-war and living artists, not pre-1945.

Flying Colours Gallery, Chelsea: 'Buy British Contemporary or Original Paintings', founded by Jane Houldsworth, thirty years of showing 'contemporary Scottish artists' plus interior design consultancy. Contemporary art gallery.

Frome Reclamation Limited, Frome, Somerset: architectural salvage and reclaimed building-materials yard (reclaimed roof tiles in clay, concrete, slate and stone, bricks, flagstones, doors, bathrooms, fireplaces, garden statuary). The site has only category pages with a one-line description each (e.g. 'Genuine garden statuary available in stone, marble, iron, and terracotta'); there is no itemised catalogue, no item prices and no online ordering, and the bulk of the business is building materials rather than antiques.

Gideon Hatch (London SW11, by appointment, LAPADA member) sells his own newly designed hand-knotted rugs made in India and Afghanistan, 'unique and bespoke ... custom made to order in all sizes and colours', from GBP 630 per square metre with a 16 to 20 week lead time (Beach House collection since 2004). New made-to-order goods, no antique stock.

Gillian Jason Gallery: 'first in the UK to solely champion female-identifying artists', representing emerging, mid-career and established living artists and estates (Megan Baker, current 2026 exhibitions). Contemporary art gallery.

Gladwell & Patterson (Burlington Arcade, est. 1746) describes itself as '19th-century, Impressionist and Post-Impressionist paintings, alongside contemporary fine art and sculpture'. Its current artworks list and artist roster show a large living-artist share (Clare Haley, Georgie Harrison, Lucy Kent, Peter Wileman, Stewart Lees, Peter Symonds and many more; roughly 40 percent of the 40 most recently added works) next to historic works (de Breanski, Jacob, Cuneo), plus a Christmas gift guide. A far-from-trivial contemporary share, not a predominantly antique stock.

Goldmark Gallery (Shopify): 'Original Art, Ceramics, Books & Prints', 50 years of knowledge; stock is mainly new work by living makers (Anne-Mette Hjortshoj teapots, mugs, platters, Morwenna Thistlethwaite) and editions of Picasso ceramics and prints, with gift ideas and vouchers. New ceramics and contemporary art.

heritage-sas.com serves an empty page; a headless-Chromium render shows a GoDaddy parked-domain placeholder ('is parked free, courtesy of GoDaddy.com', related searches for heritage conservation). No business, catalogue or contact.

Imperial Rugs (Magento shop, info@imperialrugs.co.uk) sells 'antique and decorative rugs' but its catalogue has a dedicated 'Contemporary Rugs' category and many newly made pieces: 'Tibetan wool contemporary rug' GBP 450, 'M&S Contemporary handmade wool rug limited edition', 'Liberty of London Hera Revival rug', 'Arts & crafts revival wool rug in the manner of Dresser', plus handmade decorative Milas and Oushak rugs; the about page also cites collaborations with Liberty and Burberry. New or revival goods are well above 5 percent of the catalogue.

James Hyman Gallery (James Hyman Fine Art Ltd, company 3866544, VAT 202526354): 'specialises in twentieth-century British art, with particular strength in post-war painting and the School of London', combining artist representation with a select inventory of major works. Post-war art with living-artist representation, not predominantly pre-1945; prices only on request.
JGM Gallery: 'Specialists in contemporary art by First Nations Australian and UK-based artists'; current exhibition of contemporary Indigenous artists. Contemporary art gallery.

Jill George Gallery Ltd 'represents paintings, drawings, watercolours, monoprints, limited edition prints and small sculpture by British Contemporary artists' and a commissioned series of ceramic sculptures. Contemporary art gallery.

John Bennett Fine Paintings (London; Old Master and 18th/19th-century sporting, marine, portrait and still-life paintings by Cleveley, Serres, Herring-era artists) lists 90 works but every one of the first 22 items shows 'GBP POA' and no price is given anywhere; no postal address ('London, England, UK') and no email, only a telephone number, no company details.

John Davies Gallery, Moreton-in-Marsh: 'the Cotswolds' flagship modern and contemporary gallery'; current programme is living artists (Matthew Alexander 'Years of Pilgrimage' 7 Nov - 19 Dec 2026, four-artist exhibition with Andrew Bird). Contemporary art gallery.

John Iddon Fine Art: '20th & 21st Century British Art'; the About page says he 'deals in contemporary British Art, from the 1960s to the present' (Richard Bawden, Melissa Scott-Miller, Anne Swankie, Eleanor Fein, Sonia Lawson, 'several younger contemporary artists'); most prices POA. Contemporary art.

Kaye Michie Fine Art (Richmond, Surrey; BADA/LAPADA): about 80 works in stock, 'approx. 1860-1980' watercolours and drawings. The WooCommerce catalogue (89 products, 49 'works for sale') is dominated by Modern British and living artists: 22 products by Sean Jefferson (b.1957), plus Oliver Maughan, Ray Campbell (b.1956), Terry Frost, Mary Fedden, Donald Hamilton Fraser, Bratby, Frederick Gore; Victorian works (Allingham, Birket Foster, W.H. Hunt) are a minority. Living-artist share about 25 percent and post-war share large: not predominantly pre-1945.

Lacewing Fine Art Studio (Stratford-sub-Castle, Salisbury) is a 'Fine Art Restorers and Bespoke Framers' business with restoration, advice and valuations pages; the WooCommerce store API returns 404 and there is no stock catalogue. Framing/restoration-only service.

Martyn Gregory (West Hampstead office by appointment, since 1965) deals in China Trade paintings 1700-1950; since 2023 it has no gallery and focuses on art fairs and online exhibitions. The website has only an About page and numbered PDF catalogues (catalogue 103 'George Chinnery, Artist of Macau', 2023); there is no browsable stock listing or item prices on the site.

McEwan Gallery, Ballater (Artlogic site; Scottish and European paintings from the 17th century to the present, plus 'a wide selection of contemporary and affordable works' and contemporary ceramics): the artworks list gives artist, title, medium and sizes only, no price at all (0 price strings in the page), and the stock mixes living and recent artists such as John Bellany with antique work. Auction check: none (only attends auctions as buyer).

Naval and Maritime Books (66 Royal Hill, Greenwich) is a second-hand and out-of-print naval history bookshop with GBP 5-18 books. A sample of 32 listed titles from the General Naval and Nelson categories gave publication years 1808-2005 with only 11 of 32 (about 34 percent) published before 1970; the bulk are 1970s-2000s used reference books, so the antique/vintage share is below one half.

Old Musical Instruments (Irene Bingham, 10 Willoughby Road, London NW3; successor to Tony Bingham's dealership) lists 'Old & New Books + Old Music & Methods', 'Old Musical Instruments' and 'Iconography'. Every instrument category checked (transverse flutes, duct flutes, single/double/free reeds, brass, strings, keyboards, percussion, ethnographic, miscellaneous) answers 'Sorry there are no Instruments available under this category'; the catalogue that is online is reference books (second-hand and new, 1979-2011 examples at GBP 10-30). No qualified antique stock is currently listed.

Hammered and milled coin shop on Wix (e.g. Richard III penny GBP 485, Henry VIII Irish groats GBP 585-675, John short cross penny GBP 195) with prices and Spink references, i.e. qualified stock, but no operator is identifiable: the page title says 'Devons Coins', the footer and product pages say 'devoncoins.co.uk', no proprietor or company is named (a blog post is signed 'colin stevens'), only 'Okehampton, Devon, UK' and a mobile number are given, no email and no delivery terms; copyright is '2023'. Trading name and operator cannot be stated with confidence.

Halls Hammered Coins (British hammered coins 100 BC-1662 AD, BNTA member, genuine-coin guarantee, postage page with Royal Mail rates GBP 4.86-19.95 UK, Europe GBP 12, rest of world GBP 15) is qualified stock, but the site publishes no legal operator, proprietor, postal address or place of business anywhere (about, contact, postage, links pages); only office hours and a phone/WhatsApp number. No location can be recorded. AUCTION check: the news ticker mentions 'lots of auctions this month' as sourcing of new additions, no own auctions.

Kulik Selzer (Squarespace; 20th-century French and Italian design, art, African/Oceanic art) names no legal operator or postal address and the home country is unclear: the Contact page says the offices and showroom are in 'London's historic Spitalfields neighbourhood' (no street address) while the home page and Contact page also give a New York gallery 'The Gallery 200 Lex, 200 Lexington Ave., NY 10016'; furniture prices are shown as USD 0.00 (price on request) and the art section mixes contemporary photography and paintings (Julie Blackmon 2017, Ester Nienhuis b.1977) with older works. Operator, home country and priced share cannot be established.

The site is a JavaScript single-page application ('messums', Quasar shell, empty body): the plain fetch returns an empty page and two headless-Chromium renders (60 s and 90 s) timed out with no DOM, so no stock, contact, imprint or prices could be read.

geography.addressText: Stephen Wheeler Medals, 20 Cecil Court, London, WC2N 4HE, United Kingdom

areas.assertion: Countries outside the United Kingdom served by Royal Mail; the dealer asks buyers to get in contact if a country is not served

qualification.basis: Stephen Wheeler, military medal dealer for over 40 years, trading from the shop at 20 Cecil Court, London WC2N 4HE for 20 years (open Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday, plus a Monday stall at Covent Garden antiques market). decision.basis: Hornseys, Ripon (est. 1976), rare and signed books, maps and artwork, runs a WooCommerce store of 2,857 products. Besides antique maps (470), antique artwork (253) and ephemera it sells large new-goods and contemporary parts: 232 works by contemporary artists, Lush Designs (135 products), nanoblock kits, candles, Donna Wilson gifts, 126 new teddy bears (Charlie Bears etc.), 200 Herge/Tintin items including limited-edition resin models marked Ex-Display, plus 887 books of which modern first editions and signed books form a large part. New and contemporary goods clearly exceed 5 percent, with dedicated sections.

Hungerford Arcade is a multi-dealer antiques centre ('over 100 antiques dealers under one roof', 'Our Dealers' page lists stands such as Corgi models, silver, postcards, records, a tearoom). The website is an information, newsletter and blog site (visit, directions, events, contact form); no itemised priced catalogue and no shop was found despite WooCommerce files in the theme.

Ingnet Ltd (Registered in England No. 3913090, Barnard Castle; Companies House confirms the active company) trades Arts and Crafts and Yorkshire oak furniture, Robert Mouseman Thompson pieces, watercolours and Moorcroft/Troika collectables in a WooCommerce shop (about 100 items in stock, 2,138 pages incl. sold archive). Sampled in-stock product pages carry dates: of 12 dated items only about 3 are pre-1970 (Circa 1960s lamp, 1968 watercolour, c.1920 bronze); the rest are Circa 1970, 1970, 1973, 1980s, 1988, 1990s, 1998 and Circa 2000 (Mouseman dining suites and partners desk, Moorcroft by Anji Davenport, Rachel Bishop and Vicky Lovatt, Chris Mouncey watercolours). Estimated pre-1970 share roughly 25-35 percent, below the more-than-half rule. No auction activity seen.

In Situ Manchester sells architectural salvage but its WooCommerce store (6,401 products) also has dedicated new or contemporary parts: modern stoves (Stockton multifuel convector, 'Modern stoves', 'Stoves ready to go'), traditional-style exterior doors, new timber, Olde English tiles, Neo Classic and other radiators listed separately from the 31 reclaimed radiators, and items titled Contemporary (Contemporary Arper Catifa chair, Contemporary round pedestal table, Contemporary Patrizia Garganti table lamp). A sample of 700 products shows roughly one in five as contemporary, style or new items. Dedicated new-goods sections exist.

Paul's Emporium / Islington Antiques, 386 York Way, London N7: the site states 'Most of our stock does not appear online and can only be purchased by visiting the shop'. The home page shows a feed of Instagram posts with truncated captions (no prices, no itemised catalogue pages, no shop or basket). Buying/selling and probate valuation pages are services. Shop is also described by reviewers as house clearance and vintage items.

Kendall's Fine Art lists 350 available items: 178 contemporary art works (yacht racing, wildlife, abstract, pet portraits and glass art by living artists), 67 traditional-art items, sculpture, limited-edition prints, 20th- and 21st-century furnishings and only 6 antiques. Majority is contemporary or recent art and prints by living artists.

The page states 'This website is no longer active' and only links to other sites (Antiques Boutique, a web design firm, a militaria marketplace, an eCommerce builder). No stock, contact or operator is shown.

Konstantin Antiques (Shopify, 878 products) sells antique silver spoons, Russian Empire coins and antiquities (about 608 own-vendor items) but 270 products (31 percent) are new third-party brand goods: Calvin Klein, Barbour, Bering, Mido, TW Steel and Ingersoll watches, Osprey and other leather bags, wallets, belts, perfume and room fragrance, lab-grown diamond rings. The menu has dedicated collections for perfume, bags, belts, quartz and automatic watches by brand.

L. Prentice Art & Antiques Ltd (Lillie Road, London SW6) describes itself as '20th Century Modernist Art & Design: Modern British Painters, Studio Ceramics, Mid-Century Design and Sculpture'; the about page lists mid 20th century British paintings, limited edition prints and studio pottery. The Wix catalogue of about six items has two oil portraits by Lindsay Kemp (1938-2018) with a dedicated page, a 1960s abstract oil, a Sputnik-glaze vase and mid-century design objects. Art is largely post-war modern with living-period artists; not predominantly pre-1945.

Leanne's Anime and Collectables, Great Yarmouth: Shopify shop for new official anime figures, Ichiban Kuji prizes, trading card events (One Piece, Riftbound) and Japanese gifts ('100% Official goods'). New-goods retail, no antiques or vintage stock.

lenkiewiczart.com redirects (301) to lenkiewiczartsandjewellery.com, Lenkiewicz Arts and Jewellery (Shopify, 263 products). Stock: about 45 rings (mostly modern gold and gem rings) plus necklaces, bracelets and earrings, used modern Rolex, Omega and Longines watches, 57 paintings and prints largely by Robert Lenkiewicz (1941-2002) and living artists (e.g. Sallie Gaywood), and an antique department of about 21 items. Only about 20 percent of titles name a pre-1970 date or period; estimated antique/vintage share under 35 percent. The home page also offers jewellery designs and remodelling, and a Dolce Amor jewellery collection.

LeoQuent, South Hinksey (Oxford), calls its stock 'Neo-Steptoe furniture and curios sourced from within 25 miles': a Wix shop of generic second-hand furniture and bric-a-brac with one-word titles and no dating, e.g. Chairs GBP 50, Books GBP 1, Large large bottle tops GBP 15, Towel rail, Planters pots, Cast iron railings. No antique or vintage qualification can be shown; general used goods.

Les Couilles du Chien, Notting Hill, Shopify store of decorative antiques (910 products incl. sold archive). Of the 143 available priced items measured from products.json, 39 (27 percent) are framed butterfly, insect and natural-history specimens and glass domes, 33 (23 percent) are explicitly 1970s (Murano chandeliers, perspex tables, psychedelic and band posters of the 1970s), 36 (25 percent) carry an explicit pre-1970 period (Art Deco, 19th century, 1950s, 1960s, Edwardian) and 35 are undated decorative pieces. Even if every undated piece were old the pre-1970 share stays below about half; estimated antique/vintage share about 25-50 percent.

Linktree page of Curio & Quirk, Lancaster ('Pokemon TCG, collectables, antiques, gifts, steampunk and fancy dress'); only social links and a contact link, no catalogue. The shop mixes new trading cards and gifts with antiques, and no own website with stock was found. linktr.ee itself is a third-party link-in-bio platform.

Lisseters of Bicester (family furniture shop since 1947): Google Sites page whose menu lists New Furniture, Bespoke, Beds and Mattresses, Garden furniture, Wall Mirror, Mattresses, Gifts and only one 'Preloved Furniture' section; it sells new oak, pine and painted furniture, new sofas and designer chairs. New goods dominate.

Long Melford Antiques Centre (owner Geoffrey McGregor) runs one online shop and basket for the stock of about 15 named dealer stands (dealer filter: Geoffrey McGregor, Antique Bed Shop, Martin Woolford, Brian Hawkins, John Heather, Roger Harris, David Noad, Jane Short and others); product pages read 'Showing on Geoffrey McGregor's stand' and one carries the notice that the lead image is AI generated. It is a multi-dealer antiques centre, no terms or legal operator are published, and the seller of record per item is not stated.

Lot One Ten, 78 and 78a Hoe Street, London E17 (antiques, collectables, vintage and retro bought and sold, house clearances): Wix business-card site with Home, About, Contact and an empty 'Latest new stock' page; no itemised stock or prices. The about page lists buy-in categories including house clearance, toys, coins and militaria.

Maddermarket Antiques (Shopify, 261 products) sells mostly newly made jewellery: 9ct/18ct/platinum rings with IGI-certified lab-grown diamonds, bespoke-designed solitaires, cubic zirconia studs, sterling silver bracelets and new chains. Only a few items are marked Antique. New goods far exceed 5 percent.

Militaria Buyer, 80 Derby Road, Nottingham: the home page states 'this is a Militaria Buyer Centre - it is NOT a shop and there are no items on site to come and view'. Buy-in service only, no stock for sale.

Miscellanea of Churt (est. 1980) shows 'every style from 14th century medieval to 21st century hi-tech', bespoke furniture and a contemporary showroom; its WooCommerce shop holds only 11 items and mixes antiques with new or contemporary goods: Repro Zinc Bath Planter, Contemporary Canvas Ribbon Strap Chair, 'Prima Ballerina by Isaac Kahn' signed edition 2 of 50, a hand-blown perfume bottle by a living maker. New and contemporary share is about a third.

The Mission Hall Antiques Centre, 51 The Bank, Barnard Castle: multi-dealer centre ('over forty dealers'); the static site has nine brochure pages (opening times, location, dealer stand descriptions, a few photographed items) but no itemised priced catalogue or shop.

My Tenterden is a local town business directory and events guide (accommodation, shops, events, coupons) with a category 'Antiques and Collectables'; it is a multi-merchant directory and not an antique dealer with own stock.

NerdWare, Swansea: WooCommerce shop of Pokemon trading cards (1,809 singles, current sets such as Prismatic Evolutions, Ascended Heroes, 30th Celebration). Modern collectables from the 2020s, not antiques or vintage.

North Laine Bazaar, 5-5A Upper Gardner Street, Brighton: a stall market with '50+ stalls' that invites stallholders to rent space; the one-page site (opening, address, social links) has no catalogue or priced items.

The Old Electric Shop, 'a shop of many marvellous things: books, coffee and beautiful finds': its online shop sells new gifts and accessories, e.g. handmade wool trilby hats GBP 45, a new Albero Mondo canvas notebook by Slow Design GBP 40; new goods dominate the 'Just in' section.

openstreetmap.org is the OpenStreetMap map platform; the lead is a resolved map note submitted through onosm.org for 'Timothy Langston Fine Art and Antiques' (198 Ebury Street, London SW1W 8UN, timothylangston.com). That dealer's own domain is already in the ledger (timothylangston.com, ADDED, GB); nothing to onboard from this domain.

Orangerie, 11 Great Norwood Street, Cheltenham (curated antiques and vintage): the site has Home, About, Contact and FAQ pages only, with slogans ('Antiques sublime selection, Vintage treasures galore') and a newsletter form; no itemised stock, prices or shop.

Paradox Comics, Poole (est. 1994): a comic book shop selling new comics, graphic novels and pop-culture figures and statues; the website lists 'This week's comics' only. Modern new goods and 1970s-onward nostalgia, no antique stock.

James Iles Antiques, 299 Lillie Road, London SW6 7LL (james@jiantiques.com, +44 7973 550 512; trading there 27 years): priced catalogue of about 170 items in seven categories. Titles show real antiques (18th Century French walnut commode GBP 2,200, 19th Century English fruitwood tilt-top table, Georgian tripod tables, Aesthetic Movement chairs) and mid-century pieces (1950s sectional mirror, 1960s Italian armchairs), but most lighting, mirrors, art and decorative items carry no date (Faux copper pendant lights, Travertine style ceiling lights, Verre eglomise mirrors, Blue pouffe, abstract paintings, Baroque style armchairs), and the product pages have no descriptions. The more-than-half pre-1970 share and the absence of newly made 'style' goods cannot be shown from the first-party pages. No legal operator named (copyright James Iles). Review with item-level evidence or if the owner accepts decorative-antiques dealers on title evidence.

Life of Si, 80 West St, Old Market, Bristol BS2 0BW: genuine 19th and early 20th century maps and natural-history prints ('I do not offer reproductions') in a WooCommerce shop with GBP prices and a delivery page (UK free, Europe GBP 6, rest of world GBP 8-10.50 per order). However no email address and no phone number are published on any page read (contact page is a form plus the shop address; terms and privacy name only 'Life of Si'), so the dealer cannot be onboarded. Re-check for a published email or phone.

Llewelyn and Company, 19 High Town, Hay-on-Wye HR3 5AE (phone 01497 821880; no email on the site, contact form only): Shopify catalogue of 24 products of which only 2 are in stock (22 sold out), home page headed 'Archive'. Stock is antique French kitchenalia and home decor, but several items are candles poured into antique pots and the owners' text speaks of furniture 'hen a newydd' (old and new), so the new-goods share and current stock cannot be confirmed. No legal operator published. Re-check when the shop has current stock.

Lancastrian Antiques, 70-72 Penny Street, Lancaster LA1 1XF (07977 155939, 01524 847004): the site only says 'Our website is currently undergoing a redesign' with the address and phone numbers; no stock or email is shown. Re-check after the redesign for an itemised catalogue.
