decision.basis: Past & Present Antique Centre in Risby is described as a large old wooden building 'with around 25 dealers showing their wares' (home page), stock includes costume jewellery and vintage/designer fashion. The only catalogue link (/catalogue/) is a page about a fabrics and sewing cabin; no itemised stock of one dealer is published. Multi-dealer centre without an inspectable catalogue.

Phoenix on Golborne (67 Golborne Road, London W10 5NP) shows itemised antique furniture and restored 1900-1960 lighting under 'Current stock', but the contact page and home page publish no email address and no telephone number (only the address and opening hours), the navigation also lists a 'Chalk Paint' page (paint retail not assessed) and the home page carries injected unrelated spam links. Cannot be onboarded without a published contact; review whether a contact is added.
Portobello Road Market London arcade directory: 'approximately 190 private dealers' in arcades and units; a directory of a market with many independent traders, no own stock or catalogue.
The domain serves an Indonesian online-gambling (togel) spam page titled 'DPTOTO' instead of any gallery or antiques content; no business, stock or contact of a dealer is shown.

Puces London (271 Lillie Road SW6 7LL; terms by 'Puces LTD', GoDaddy site) shows a few priced items per category page (Louis Vuitton and Goyard trunks, easels, Art Nouveau table, Barbizon landscape, Rouault etching) but also a 'Shadow Boxes - Unique Dioramas by Puces' section of the dealer's own constructions, 'Models & Meccano' and 'The Boys' collectibles, and a Modern Paintings category; the pages carry very little text, so the share of antique/vintage versus own-made or modern pieces cannot be established with confidence.

Quindry (283 Lillie Road, London SW6 7LL; Margin Scheme dealer, VAT GB108473320) sells furniture, objects, art and lighting with prices on Webflow, but item pages carry only a title and price without any dating (e.g. 'A Pair of 1940s Oak Chairs', 'A Modernist Plinth', 'A Pair of Rizzo Cabinets', 'A Royere-inspired Daybed'). The About page says it 'tends to specialise in twentieth century design' and only sometimes adds earlier pieces, so the share made before about 1970 (and any 1970s or inspired-by pieces) cannot be established; no legal operator is named.

Reginald Ballum, Worthing (WooCommerce, 371 products via the Store API): eclectic industrial, vintage and decorative shop. About 20 products (5.4 percent) are explicitly newly made, bespoke or 'in the style of': 8 'Bespoke' pieces (lamps from temple capitals, pine drawers described as sympathetically built, sconces from salvaged fuse boxes), industrial leather armchairs described as 'mid 21st century' handmade in the style of Casa Padrino, plus further modern club sofas, bar stools and a jute floor vase without any age; with these the new-goods share is estimated at 6 to 9 percent, above the 5 percent tolerance (BORDERLINE: the rest is mostly antique and vintage).

Remains to be Seen, 24 East Street, Ilminster, is a shop where 'a number of dealers offer a diverse range of items'; the site only has photo galleries of dealers' cabinets, no itemised priced stock of one operator.

Shopify retailer of new trading cards (Magic: The Gathering Secret Lair, Pokemon graded slabs, new sets), new Dragon Shield sleeves and video games; modern new goods, not antiques or pre-1970 vintage.

Richard Scott Antiques, 30 High Street, Holt, is a one-page business card (address, opening hours, 'English 18th and 19th century ceramics and glass, oak and country furniture, pictures and prints', contact Luke Scott); no itemised stock or catalogue is published.

Rippingales Antiques and Collectables, Clare (Wix): home, 'Our Range' (generic list of ceramics, jewellery, silver, furniture) and an empty 'For Sale' page with a heading only; no itemised stock. The site also promotes R&R Suffolk Auctions, a pop-up auction (separate side activity, not assessed further).

Rolfeys: the workmans yard is permanently closed, the owner sells at antique and flea markets and offers probate, house clearance and valuation services; the site says items will be offered 'soon' through the website but publishes no shop or catalogue.

Rose Lane (Wix) is a lifestyle and interior brand ('started as an independent shop in St Ives selling art, ephemera and antiques', now based at a farm opening 2026); pages are about, blog, press and interiors, with no itemised stock or catalogue.

Scotmint (coins, medals, militaria and banknotes, own shop.php catalogue): the coin department alone lists 2,436 items, sampled pages show modern Royal Mint proof and brilliant uncirculated pound coins (1991-1994), 2007 silver proof sets and banknotes dated 2002 and 2021 next to old coins, medals and 1930s-50s notes; the home page also advertises modern coins, proof sets, uncirculated sets and Royal Mint coins as a department. Modern-issue stock is far above the 5 percent tolerance.

Scottish Antique and Arts Centres (Abernyte and Doune) are multi-dealer centres with 'over 100 dealers'; the only online shop is 'Templemans', 'stylish contemporary furniture, home accessories and gifts' (WooCommerce) with packaging and damage terms for its furniture range, and no itemised antique stock of any dealer is published.
Shirehall Plain Antiques Centre, Holt: nine showrooms with 'over 20 antiques dealers'; the website offers a photo gallery ('just a small sample') and no itemised, priced stock of a single operator.

The London Silver Vaults is a shopping destination of independent dealers ('Meet the Shops'); the site is a directory of the vault's shops and offers antique, modern and contemporary silverware by many traders, not one dealer's own stock.

Sivyers Antiques Emporium and Auction House, Bexhill: the site is led by monthly general auctions (20 percent buyer and seller commission, absentee and phone bidding, consignments accepted for 8 January 2027) and the 'Antiques Emporium' is a venue for more than 20 stallholders plus a framing service, with no itemised own-stock catalogue; auction house is the main identity.

skout, Stockbridge Edinburgh: 'curated second hand goods, collectibles and curiosities' spanning homeware, jewellery, apparel, vintage and antiques; general second-hand retail without a qualified majority of antique or pre-1970 stock.

Society for the Protection of Unwanted Objects (125 Emporium, Dulwich Road, Weebly): a mixed shop of retro, antique and reclaimed industrial furniture, vintage clothes, 'some new art', new ceramics and jewellery 'old and new'; pages are about, contact and blog only, no itemised stock.

Staveley Antiques, Kendal: descriptive pages on restored antique beds, lighting and cast-iron radiators ('give John a call', 'email for details', mattresses with price list on request); no itemised priced stock, only illustrative photos and captions.

Stevie's Wonders Antiques, Rye: the own site is a brochure (about, policies, Instagram) without a catalogue; selected pieces are sold online only through a collaboration with Odloft, a separate curated furniture shop (marketplace stock).

Stick Antiques and Vintage, Lostwithiel: the About page says 'I do not sell online at present'; the product gallery shows only a few featured items (Troika vase, Clarice Cliff sugar shaker) and the shop also holds 'new decorative items'.

Streett Marburg (Shopify, 2,480 products via /products.json, 338 available): 156 of the available items (46 percent) are 'Cushions, bolsters' newly made by the dealer from antique linens and lace ('To order', feather filler included), and about 30 available items are contemporary abstract artworks (JC Cotton, dated 2026; Lucy Naughton) in antique frames; many further items are 1970s pieces. New-made and contemporary stock is far above the 5 percent tolerance.
Swans Head, Alston: 'vintage/antique and local craft items' shop; the online store page renders no products (empty product list with 'search term not specific enough'), so no stock can be inspected.
Tara Antiques, The Manor House, Stow-on-the-Wold: 'around 30 dealers' on three floors with a virtual tour and image gallery; no itemised priced stock of one operator.

Patricia Harvey Antiques (ph9 antiques platform) has a dedicated 'Anna Scholz Ceramics' section of new pieces by a living ceramic artist (Kyoto bowl, lamp and vase, GBP 95-850) next to antique furniture, fabrics and books; the dedicated new-goods section exceeds the tolerance for new goods.

The Antiques Emporium, Kendal (Cumbria) is a walk-in antiques centre with over 50 traders. The Squarespace site has only home, blog, things-to-do and contact pages; no catalogue, product listing or itemised stock is published online. Not a single dealer selling own itemised stock.

Levenshulme Antiques Village (Greater Manchester) is a multi-dealer antiques hypermarket (pages: Dealers, Rent a Unit, Opening times, Gallery). No online catalogue or itemised priced stock is published; visitors are directed to the premises.

The Bourne Mill, Farnham is a six-floor centre of over 70 independent traders. The site has no catalogue of its own; its 'Online Shop' menu entry links to bournemill.etsy.com (Etsy marketplace). Stock is multi-trader and the only online selling channel is a third-party marketplace.

The Chapel, Pembroke (Wix): Furniture, Garden and Interiors 'galleries' are photo galleries with category prose (blanket boxes, dressers, wardrobes...) and no item titles, descriptions, dimensions or prices. No itemised stock to inspect.

The Collecterie, Teddington: webshop of interiors, gifts, decorative accessories, stationery and bathroom essentials (e.g. etched wine glass GBP 14, feather spoon GBP 6, flat bear, notebooks) - new-goods retail with no antique stock evident. Policy: new goods well above 5%.

The Collector Antiques, Barnard Castle is an art and furniture restoration service; the 'For Sale' page contains only About/Contact text (25 The Bank, DL12 8PH) and no itemised items for sale. Restoration-only service.

The Cowshed, Carisbrooke (Isle of Wight): WooCommerce Store API lists 544 products; the 'Rugs' category alone holds 112 items (about 21%), described e.g. 'Stunning rug for a contemporary look' with new-rug names (Poodle rug, Aztec rug), plus gifts and new decorative lines. Antique pine furniture exists but the new-goods share is far above the 5% limit.

The FM Gallery, London NW8: 791 WooCommerce items of 20th/21st-century Italian design. The About page says it champions 'established and emerging designers, architects, artists' and the sampled catalogue holds new pieces (2020 Spider Special Edition ceiling light by Diego Mardegan, 2022 resin sculptures, Vitra Eames soft pads, SACS glass by Silvano Signoretto) next to many 1970s-1980s items; a majority of pre-1970 stock cannot be shown and a new/contemporary share is evident.

The Nutshell Warwick, Old Post Office, Old Square: one-page WordPress site (opening times, contact) for a shop of vintage watches, clocks, collectables and curios. No catalogue, product listing or WooCommerce store API (404) is published.

The old Chemist Shop Antiques Centre, 206 Mill Road, Cambridge (GoDaddy store, rendered with headless Chromium): about 100 undated general items (Nikon F60 and Canon EOS cameras and lenses, record player, Newton's cradle, gloves, shot glasses, pendant lights); prices GBP 8-140, no periods or makers given. A majority of pre-1970 antique or vintage stock cannot be shown; reads as a general second-hand mix.

The Old Flight House, Weston on the Green is a 6,000 sq ft centre with over 70 independent unit holders plus cafe and flower shop; pages Antiques/Vintage/Interiors/Cafe/Visit Us describe the premises only. No online catalogue or itemised stock.

The Pumping Station, Cardiff: multi-trader antiques centre (Traders page lists independent stallholders by phone: Llantwit Antiques, Sully Antiques, Aunty's Attic...). Category pages and a photo gallery only; no itemised or priced online stock.
The Retro Retreat, King's Lynn: Pokemon trading cards, grading service, games and tech (new booster boxes, collection boxes); not antiques or vintage dealer stock.
The SHED, Sproughton (Suffolk): four showrooms of multi-dealer antiques, vintage and fashion with a tearoom, boutique and teddy bear hospital; Wix site without any catalogue or itemised stock.

The Swan at Tetsworth: auctioneer-led operation; the home page leads with monthly auctions (next auction 2 December, catalogue on the-saleroom), valuations and probate; the antique market/centre is a multi-dealer addition. Auctions are its main identity (policy B (a)).

The Vintage Trading Post (Tytherleigh and Ottery St Mary, Devon): multi-trader pitches (Vintage Card, Ghost Records, Alices Attic, Carols Vintage, Andymart Retro...) shown as photos only; the only WooCommerce categories are Colourman paint and a deal of the week (new goods). No itemised antique stock.

Trader's Antiques, 131 Grosvenor Road, Aldershot (Wix): the Store, Furniture, Doors, Collectibles, Militaria and Pictures pages show only category headings with no itemised stock; the contact page says 'at the present time, we are open by arrangement'; the shop link points to tradersantiques.etsy.com. The site also lists gifts and a wood sale.

Treasure Trove East Grinstead (Felbridge): self-described eco-friendly house clearance shop for second-hand furniture, household items and collectibles (Lladro, Portmeirion); eco-clearance model, no itemised online catalogue.
Vee Bee's Interiors: new luxury homeware boutique (faux flowers, candles, diffusers, wall art, soft furnishings, new furniture and lighting); no antique stock.

Waterside Antiques, Ely: antiques centre with more than 65-80 independent dealers (about page); the site offers only a small 'stock viewer' of sample items (for example a Tuscan decoro painted jug GBP 22) from many dealers, not an itemised catalogue of one operator's own stock.

Flea Circus, Newcastle: department store of local independent creatives, makers and sellers (furniture, fashion, music, art, homewares; 'vintage and contemporary'); multi-vendor shop floor with no online catalogue.

Welsh Bridge Books & Collectables, Shrewsbury: single-page site for a three-floor second-hand bookshop; the only online selling is 'a little online via eBay & Abebooks' (links to marketplace storefronts); the own site holds no catalogue.
World Of Stuff, Horsforth (Shopify): the 'Buy stuff' menu reads 'Coming soon', and /products.json holds 0 products; no itemised stock is published.

Worth a Look, Shanklin: general store (SumUp online store) of postcards, collectibles, books, CDs, fishing tackle and rigs, bath bombs, batteries, craft kits, incense and homeware; new goods dominate.
Lead URL was a Facebook page; ynotantiques.co.uk itself redirects to https://www.facebook.com/ynotantiques/ (Stratford-upon-Avon). No own website or itemised stock.

Asylum Books & Games: WooCommerce shop of about 120,000 modern comic back issues, graphic novels, statues and posters (e.g. X-Men Vol. 6 issues at GBP 4.75-12.50); modern collectibles/new goods, not antiques or pre-1970 vintage.

Unique Antique Shop (Shopify, 131 products, antique and vintage ceramics, bronzes, furniture; updated catalogue) names no legal operator and publishes no email address or phone number: the contact page is a form only, About names Martin and Gina and a Dovercourt (Harwich) shop without an address, the privacy policy gives only a data protection representative address (1 Bullfinch Close, Dovercourt, CO12 4WH; possibly private). Cannot onboard without a published contact.

The Vintage Watch Company, Burlington Arcade London: over 2,000 vintage Rolex wristwatches 'c1910-c2000' (sampled listings: sport Rolex 1957-1979, ladies 1963-1980, early vintage 1920s-1990s, with many 1980s-1990s pieces). The pre-1970 share could not be measured from the JS-driven listing pages and may be below half; no legal operator or company number is published (owners John and David Silver named), and the site also sells a new book. Defer until the age share and operator can be confirmed.

Warehams, 68 Oxford Street, Whitstable: itemised stock of garden ornaments and furniture with prices (e.g. GBP 750 Young Bacchus). Many items are undated cast/composite stone or reproductions in the style of antiques ('Cast stone Bacchus figure based on the original by Michelangelo', 'Large Victorian style planter', cast stone dragon finials, hand painted penguins, one page still reads 'NEED DESCRIPTION'), alongside dated antiques (Blashfield planters c1860, cast iron urns c1870, fountain c1920, Ercol, Willy Guhl 1950-60). Williams & Parfitt Antiques and Interiors, 7 Middleton Street, Wymondham (Shopify, 289 products, about 72% age-hinted antique/vintage). The antiques centre has over 30 independent dealers; 111 of 289 online products carry other dealers' vendor names (No12antiques, Norfolk Vintiques, ACE Collectables, Avocet Antiques, Lines and Son...). No terms/delivery page exists (policies 404), the contact page is a form without email, and it is unclear who is the seller of record for those items. Defer until terms show whether the centre sells them in its own name (commission is acceptable) or merely lists third parties.

Lead thethriftygent.co.uk redirects to https://www.desiredlifestyle.co.uk/ where 'DESIRED ANTIQUES & INTERIORS LTD' shows only 'This website is no longer active' with links to other websites of interest (antiquesboutique.com, militariazone.com). Itemised catalogue of 430 priced pieces (280 currently in stock; sold items archived) in 13 categories, e.g. 'Gilt carved eagle console table' GBP 10,250, '19th-Century French Rouge Marble Mantel Clock' GBP 2,220, 'Victorian Pitch Pine Refectory Centre Table' GBP 800. Roughly half of the in-stock titles name an antique era (Victorian, Georgian, Regency, 18th/19th century, Art Deco) and about 8 percent are 1970s+ vintage or 'style of' decorative pieces; the rest are undated period furniture and objects. Estimated majority antique/vintage; BORDERLINE because the exact pre-1970 share is not stated. No auctions, no contemporary-art stock beyond a few late 20th-century paintings, no new-goods section. Delivery included in prices to mainland England and Wales (GBP 25 extra inside the M25 and low-emission zones).

omissions: No street address is published on the site (template shows only 'Tetbury'): the only location is the Companies House registered office of the company named in the privacy policy, with no showroom, pickup or inventory claim

Delivery to mainland England and Wales is stated as included in prices with a GBP 25 surcharge inside the M25/low-emission zones and 'additional charges outside this area': shipping is asserted only as partial England/Wales delivery without a rate because the surcharge zones and mainland limit cannot be represented; international delivery is on quote and not asserted

decision.basis: Harrison Antique Furniture, Stratford-upon-Avon (est. 2009; 07976 001331, harrisonantiquefurniture@gmail.com): online shop of 'Antique & Old Reproduction furniture', retro design furniture and 'traditional craftsman made Reproduction furniture' alongside Edwardian to Georgian antiques. In the home-page selection of about 38 pieces, roughly 15 are described as reproduction or 'style' pieces (Georgian Style Mahogany Extending Dining Table, Tudor Style Oak Blanket Chest, Louis Style bedroom suite, Mahogany Bookcase Cabinet by Reprodux, Reproduction Oak Carved Sideboard Base, Hines of Oxford and Parker Knoll retro pieces) and a Guinness barrel cocktail cabinet; the genuine antiques named are a minority, so a majority of antique or pre-1970 stock is not shown. Carts use index.asp GET add links (not followed).

Hermitage Antiques, 37 High St, Honiton EX14 1PW (hermitageantiqueshoniton@gmail.com, 01404 361918 / 07925 302812; owner Alex, previously The Character Mirror Company): antique mirrors, furniture and decorative antiques plus gilding workshop. The WordPress custom post type 'antiques' (REST) holds 13 itemised entries with reference numbers, measurements and period descriptions (Louis XVI reeded mirror c1800, Regency convex mirror c1820, late 19th-century smokers bow armchair) but no prices, and every item page checked (9 of 13 opened) is marked SOLD; the rendered Stock page and home 'Latest Honiton Antiques' list show no current items, and the site says not all stock reaches the website. No current priced or unsold listing can be inspected. Re-check when new items appear.

decision.basis: Josephine Ryan Antiques, 44 Long Street, Tetbury GL8 8AQ (jryanantiques@aol.com, +44 7973 336149), Shopify site. The product feed (500 entries) consists of photo-only entries titled '.' with product types such as 'Sold', 'paintings', 'Mirrors' and 'seating', price 0.00 and no description, period, maker or measurements; each product page only says 'if you are interested in this item, please fill in the form below'. The catalogue is a photo gallery without item data, so no identifiable itemised stock can be inspected (not merely missing prices).

Artemis Vintage (Square Online site): rendered home shows featured categories 'Artemis Vintage', 'Boho Bella' and 'Upcycled Tinkerings' (boho/upcycled vintage-style goods), a Square placeholder location (2510 Eastern Boulevard, York, PA 17402, phone (555) 555-5555, hi@mystore.com) and no UK imprint, so neither a GB business nor a specialist antiques dealer can be established; the shop policy says all items are sold as-is, no returns. No antiques stock or GB operator shown.

Ludlow Vintage, 5 Corve St, Ludlow SY8 1DA. Home page carries a closure notice for the shop (last trading day Saturday 23rd August) and says vintage pieces would continue online 'for the foreseeable future'. Rendered all five shop categories (glassware, furniture, ceramics, lighting, home decor) on 2026-11-27: every category shows 'No results to display', so no stock is itemised. Stock when trading was 20th-century furniture incl. post-modern/contemporary. No legal operator named. Nothing to onboard; revisit only if a catalogue reappears.

Old Town Magick, Edinburgh (Shopify). Public products.json (3 pages fetched) lists 750 products, all product_type 'Art Print', all tagged UNFRAMED/Wall Art Print, 666 tagged 'New', sourced from museum open-access collections (tags met-open-access, nga-open-access): newly produced reproduction wall-art prints, plus Christmas cards and notebooks. Antiques are only a small 'Vintage & Antiques' menu entry. A shop selling new prints and decorative wall art is out of scope (contemporary art / new-goods policy). No imprint operator checked further.

Pastorale Antiques, 15 Malling Street, Lewes BN7 2RA (Wix). Home page states '9 dealers showcasing antiques from 16th century to midcentury' in a multi-dealer antiques centre with a licensed courtyard cafe, a tile showroom and the separate Snake Hips Vintage (designer fashion). The 'Latest Stock' page is only an Instagram embed; no itemised online catalogue (rendered with headless Chromium). About text also mentions repro and modern original paintings. Multi-dealer centre without an own inspectable catalogue.

Ludlow Period House Shop (periodhouseshops.com, Ludlow, tel 01584 877276). Menu: Lighting, Homeware, Bathrooms, Radiators, Door Furniture & Ironmongery, Clothing, Brands, Garden, Kitchen Fittings. It is a new-goods retailer of period-style fittings and brand products; 'Antiques and Salvage' and 'antique-salvaged' lighting are only one sub-section among many new-goods departments (new share far above 5%).

puritanvalues.co.uk answers HTTP 301 to https://www.puritanvalues.com/ (checked 2026-11-27). puritanvalues.com (Puritan Values Limited, Southwold; Arts and Crafts / Aesthetic Movement specialists) is already ADDED in the GB ledger (listing source ls_01m8cy9gkheaqawems50b7b2dg, Party pty_01m8cy9gkceqvapmnf5xvyxvcj; same email info@puritanvalues.com and phone +447966371676 as published on the dealer's contact page). No second Party or source.

Second To None Stamford (Neil Scholes, warehouse Old Great Road, Stamford PE9 2XT, online only). Self-described 'one of the largest online secondhand shops' with 1,000+ items: categories Furniture, Electricals, Rugs/Flooring/Curtains, Garden & DIY, Everything Else. Items-for-sale page shows general second-hand goods at GBP 3-165 (plastic suitcases, kettles, paper shredders, mobility aids, ladders, modern Habitat dining sets, divan bases); the occasional 1930s oak bureau is a small minority (well under half antique/vintage). House-clearance business.

Sofiko, 5 Henrietta Street, Cheltenham GL50 4AA. 'Vintage and retro store' that buys games, toys and retro items; site (WordPress, 3 pages) has no itemised catalogue or prices, only what-we-buy, store-location and contact pages. Retro games/toys are 1970s-onward nostalgia goods, not antique/vintage before about 1970.

Spirit of France Antiques: a Wix mini-site of a stall/exhibition space inside Stratford Antiques & Interiors (multi-dealer antiques centre, Dodwell Trading Estate, Stratford-upon-Avon CV37 9ST). Category pages (Furniture, Garden, Interior, Mirrors & Pictures, Decorative Items, Silver) are photo galleries; rendered with headless Chromium they show no item titles, descriptions, periods or prices. No operator named. Stock is not itemised.

Tallulah Fox, Lombard Street, Petworth (WordPress/WooCommerce). Menu has 'Furniture & Antiques' (antique commodes, painted cupboards, farmhouse tables, much sourced in Italy) next to a full 'Home Decor' department of new goods: designer cushions and throws, baskets, Indian reverse paintings on glass, brands Addison Ross, Boncoeurs, Charles Farris, Ester & Erik, &Klevering. Dedicated new-goods department, so NEW_GOODS_MIX.

The Flea, Cheltenham: 'Vintage & Second Hand Shop' run to raise money for The Butterfly Garden charity. One-page 123-reg website consisting of Instagram post text (sale on contemporary upholstered dining set, mid-century sideboard, Annie Sloan painted headboard, old radios, books); no itemised catalogue, no prices list, items sold in store or on Etsy. General second-hand goods.

The Old Barn, Unit C, Campend Farm, Old Dalkeith Rd, Edinburgh EH22 1RS. Wix site: antique/vintage and pine furniture (many 'upcycled' pieces) alongside separate 'Homeware & Gifts' department, 'Fusion Mineral Paint' / upcycling supplies, workshop tickets, studio hire, craft parties and gift cards. Dedicated new-goods and services sections, plus pine furniture of unclear age.

Top Banana Antiques Mall, 1 New Church Street, Tetbury GL8 8DS (Shopify). About page: the Tetbury shop 'is a Mall in the true sense. We have over 50 dealers'; contact page footer: 'V. C. Antiques (Trading as Top Banana Antiques) acts as agent on behalf of the Dealers'; 'Dealer Login' link. Online catalogue lists stock of many third-party dealers sold by an agent, so no single dealer owns the stock.

Tore Schotte Antiques, The Old Bakehouse, Blackmill Road, Southwold IP18 6AQ. WordPress site (footer (c) 2023) shows six 'Examples of stock' (oil painting, Art Deco lamp, gilded brass frame, silhouette, watercolour, gilded dolphins) as uncategorised blog posts without prices; text says 'Purchases in store during trading hours only' (shop open Thursday and Saturday). No itemised catalogue or online purchase.

Troubridge Antique & Interior Consultants (Cheltenham, tel 01242 520276). Service-led site: buying, valuations, restoration, removals, house clearance, interior consulting, security consultant, gold and silver bought. The 'Antiques Showroom' page lists four items (games table, heart table, rocking horse, side table), all marked 'Out of Stock'; no priced stock is offered. No operator or postal address published.

twinpillartables.co.uk is an older, stale site of Roger King Antiques (111 High Street, Hungerford RG17 0NB; footer 'Copyright 2017 Roger King Antiques Company Ltd.'; index.html last modified 2021-12-16; category pages such as /armchairs.html and /diningtables.html answer HTTP 404; only five dining tables shown). The same operator is already ADDED via kingantiques.co.uk (Party pty_01m8d3hx40efernygr5gfrkaya, phone +441488682256, Hungerford). No second source for a dead duplicate storefront.

Vintage Tom, online business of Charles Hart Ltd / Charles Hart Jewellers (4 Cheap Street, Frome BA11 1BN; high-street family jeweller since 1820; also buys Rolex/Omega watches). Public Shopify products.json: 1,249 products (390 tagged 'sold'); age tags 'post 1950' 406 vs 'pre 1950' 178, 183 tagged 'modern engagement rings', 55 tagged 'new', many 9ct/18ct diamond rings; shop describes 'pre-owned jewellery' incl. 'near new or modern'. Antique/vintage (before about 1970) is well below half of the catalogue.

York Minster Antiques (Jon Braganza; email and mobile only, no postal address published; Wix Stores). Catalogue of dated antique silver (York silver, pre-1850, Georgian, Art Deco, small silver, flatware; roughly 150 priced items across categories) BUT with a dedicated new-goods section: home page 'Newly created hand crafted jewellery, silverware and ornaments', category 'Silver by Jon Braganza' (own workshops, hand made trinket boxes, spoons, pendants) mirrored in 'Contemporary silver', plus a commissions/silversmithing service. Dedicated new-goods section counts as NEW_GOODS_MIX.

A.A. Zelley Ltd (Zelley Jewellers), 35 St Giles Street, Norwich NR2 1JN (Wix). Family retail jeweller that 'moved into antique and pre-owned articles' from the 1990s. Rendered shop page parsed 148 items: only 43 (29%) carry an era word (Antique, Victorian, Georgian, Edwardian, Art Deco, Vintage, 1920s); the rest are plain gold/platinum wedding bands, engagement rings, hoops, studs and dog clips with no stated age, and the site has a 'Handmade' category. Antique/vintage is not shown to be more than half of the stock.

Norah's Antiques, 15 Turl Street, Oxford OX1 3DQ (VAT GB364511703; antiques-web-design platform). About page: 'antique, vintage and antique-style jewellery ... a piece inspired by the past but made to be worn today'. Parsed 117 priced items from seven category pages: only 26 (22%) carry an era word; the large rest are new sterling-silver pieces with cubic zirconia, marcasite, topaz and agate (e.g. 'Sterling Silver, Sapphire and CZ Cluster Ring', 'Silver Dragon Pendant', 'Silver robin ring') of recent manufacture. New-goods share far above 5%.

Glasgow Architectural Salvage, Albion Industrial Complex, 1394 South Street, Glasgow G14 0AP (Square Online; tel 0141 958 1113). Salvage yard of doors, radiators, fireplaces, church pews, sanitary ware. Doors and radiators pages describe style types ('please phone quoting a style and we'll have a look to see what we've got'); only a few 'special mention' items are itemised, without prices; the 'Online Shop' page rendered with headless Chromium shows no itemised priced products, only shipping terms (postage capped at GBP 3.95, free over GBP 100). Stock is not itemised/priced for online browsing; yard stock includes hospital/school fittings of mixed age.

junkshopantiques.com answers HTTP 301 to https://www.vikiknott.com/ (Viki Knott Gallery, The Basement, 2 Hutchison Terrace, Edinburgh EH14 1QB; Shopify). L'Authentique, 5 Station Road, Southwold IP18 6AX (Wix Stores; 176 products of antique and vintage decorative items, e.g. Black Forest mirror GBP 139, antique French shop mannequin GBP 325; shop open Saturdays 10-4 and by appointment; tel 07584 314888, sales@l-authentique.co.uk). Stock would qualify, but no legal operator is named anywhere, and the privacy policy states the site content is 'the intellectual property of Attik Antiques', a name appearing nowhere else (not a live Party, no domain known); one web search found nothing. The imprint-vs-policy name conflict prevents a reliable operator fact.

decision.basis: 20th Century Glass (Wayne Stephens, Bolton; Zen Cart shop, 814 itemised products, GBP prices, UK postage free, tiered overseas rates, also eBay/Etsy channels). Genuine collectable glass dealer, but the antique/vintage (pre-1970) share cannot be established above 50%: a title scan of 566 of the 814 listings found about 45% with clear pre-1970 markers (Victorian, Art Deco, Art Nouveau, 1930s-1960s makers), about 23% with 1970s+ markers (Wedgwood glass birds, Langham, Tweedsmuir, Kosta Boda Rhapsody, Caithness, Isle of Wight, Okra, Robert Held studio glass, books) and about 32% undated vintage Murano/Mdina/Czech pieces whose date cannot be told from the title. No auctions, no new goods, no contemporary art seen. Operator is a sole proprietor with no company form; address 12 Carron Grove, Bolton BL2 6LR (contact page; returns page prints BL2 3QB - conflicting postcode) and an email obfuscated by Cloudflare, no phone. Deferred rather than guessed.

Handicraft Antiques Limited (company no. 09470132, Helvellyn, Clifton, Cumbria CA10 2EG; showroom by appointment at that address; handicraft.antiques@icloud.com, 07446 274192; Shopify) sells Arts and Crafts furniture. The Shopify feed holds 475 products but only 11 are currently available (the rest is a sold archive, 12 including a newsletter pseudo-product). The majority-antique/vintage test (before about 1970) cannot be established: of 475 titles 91 carry a date before 1970, 66 a date from 1970 or later (e.g. Stickley Mission pieces dated 2001, Treske armchairs c.1980, a 'post 1990' Knight chair, Peter Hall 'handmade contemporary' bookcase) and 318 are undated; about 120 listings are Mouseman or ex-Mouseman Yorkshire School furniture whose dates run from the 1930s to the 1990s, and of the 11 available items about half predate 1970. No auctions seen; contemporary and post-1970 workshop pieces are a significant share rather than trivial. Deferred for a stock-date review rather than guessed.

ArtsOnline (artsonline.org.uk; GoDaddy online store of about 45 pages of 15 listings, administration office Somerset Street, Bristol BS2 8NB, proprietor Aaron Thomas, artsonline@hotmail.com, 01749 595 507) is a mixed art and decorative-goods seller. A 60-listing sample across four pages shows roughly 55 percent 19th-century or earlier antiques but also about 20 percent new or post-1970 goods: dedicated 'Contemporary', 'Abstract' and 'Prints' categories with living artists (Linda Le Kinff b.1949 limited-edition silkscreens, Sarah Jane Szikora b.1971 limited-edition print 32/295, Antonio Ferri b.1938, 'Contemporary' still lifes and acrylic abstracts), 1972/1974 'vintage' paintings, and newly made decorative pieces ('Decorative Metal Medieval Knights', 'French Contemporary Figural Antique Style' bronze, Egyptian Revival bronze candelabra). The non-antique and new-goods share clearly exceeds the 5 percent tolerance and there are dedicated contemporary sections.

Banwells (Sidmouth, County House; Shopify, 509 products, 294 available) describes itself as jewellers specialising in 'fine antique, contemporary and bespoke jewellery' and offers restorations and bespoke commissions. The catalogue contains a dedicated 'Main Contemporary Collection' product type and a 'NEW IN' type next to antique pieces (e.g. Edwardian turquoise and diamond horseshoe brooch GBP 375, Victorian silver scent bottle GBP 165); many listings are modern stone-set jewellery (opal studs, emerald cluster earrings, solitaire pendants) and new retail. A contemporary/new jewellery line is a dedicated section, so the antique/vintage-only requirement is not met.

Bijou Books (Wix site; bookshop at the Pumping Station, Penarth Road, Cardiff CF11 8TT, 'more than 1500 books') is a general second-hand and modern book shop: the About page says 'every bookshelf needs its modern books' and the featured listings are used modern titles (Toni Morrison's Beloved, Ray Bradbury's The Martian Chronicles, Caitlin Thomas); antique/rare editions, Folio Society (modern reprints) and Heritage Press/Limited Editions Club sections are only part of the stock, so the majority is not antique or pre-1970 vintage. UK Silver Exchange, part of West Country Precious Metals (co-owners Steve Mangeng and Jason Knape, set up 2024 with a direct refinery link): a precious-metals trader that buys scrap and antique silver and gold and quotes bullion prices. Not a dealer selling an itemised antique stock.

Newly made goods, not antique stock; home country not established from the site.

decision.basis: Jillings Antiques, Llandrindod Wells (Powys): an antique clock and barometer repair and restoration workshop (35+ years, BWCMG member) with 'a small showroom where we exhibit some of our own restored stock'. The site has no itemised catalogue: the 'repair & sales' page is repair text plus an unlabelled photo gallery (image file names only, no titles, periods or prices), and there is no shop or product pages. Restoration service with a showroom mention only, so no inspectable stock.

Cawarden Reclaim (Staffordshire, WooCommerce shop): reclaimed building materials merchant, home page leads with '1.5M+ reclaimed bricks', tiles, flooring, beams, kerbs and chimney pots; furniture and garden items are 'reclaimed and new in stock'. A builders' reclamation yard, not an antiques or vintage dealer; new goods are sold alongside.

Cheshire Demolition: demolition, excavation, skip hire, recycling and aggregates business; its 'reclamation yard' (architectural salvage, chimney pots, building materials) is described only in text and blog posts, with no itemised antique stock. Not an antiques dealer.

Jim Wise Reclamation (Burslem, Stoke-on-Trent, Shopify): 5 acre reclamation yard selling reclaimed bricks, roof tiles, slate, ridge tiles, pantiles, timber and chimney pots to builders and the public; sister company of Jim Wise Demolition. Building-materials reclamation, not an antiques or vintage dealer.

Cullens of Surrey (Sutton/Surrey): the home page presents an 'online auction house & secondhand collectable shop' with Auctions, Buying at Auction and Selling at Auction as the main menu, plus probate and house-clearance services; the shop is the retail corner of an auction and clearance business (policy B a/e). Its goods are described as second-hand antiques, retro goods and collectables, so the general second-hand scope would not qualify either.

CJ's Classic Cameras: a private vintage-camera collection and repair-notes website of an amateur collector near Edinburgh ('my collection of vintage cameras ... set up mainly to keep track of my cameras for myself'). No items are offered for sale, no shop and no prices; the links page only lists other vintage camera shops.

Comet Classics (Portsmouth area, PO12): used classic motorcycle and scooter dealer, 'over 100 classic motorcycles and petrol pumps', by appointment. The itemised stock is motor vehicles of mixed age (e.g. 1999 Kawasaki ZZR600, 1973 Honda 750/4, 1961 Triumph Bonneville and Lambretta) sold through a Bikes in Stock feed; the petrol-pump page lists no items ('please call us for details'). A vehicle dealer, not an antiques or vintage-objects dealer, and much of the stock is post-1970.

Film Camera Store (UK, Shopify): products.json lists 1,250 products (731 available), almost all used consumer film cameras and lenses of the 1970s to 2000s (210 point-and-shoots, 70 SLRs, 29 compact digital cameras, flashes, straps and manuals) with new items mixed in (film bundles, disposable cameras, 'Brand New KUGO' camera). Almost nothing is dated before 1970; used consumer electronics rather than antiques or pre-1970 vintage.

Jardinopia (jardinopia.com redirects to jardinopia.co.uk, Shopify): the catalogue holds 1,114 products (910 available) of which roughly a quarter are newly made home, garden and seasonal goods sold under the vendor 'Jardinopia Home And Garden' (Christmas decorations 156, planters, plant stakes, cushions, diffusers, face masks, wall art), alongside Indian antique and vintage architectural pieces (doors, gates, teak furniture). Far above the 5 percent new-goods limit.

Fergus & Gibbs Ltd (CRN 13704511, registered office Drinkstone, Bury St Edmunds IP30 9SY; Wix store, 125 product pages): petroliana, enamel signs, automobilia, aviation salvage and militaria sold from a 'Finds Yard' at fixed prices or on request, with some finds sent to auction through the owners' own eBay shop (AUCTION SIDE ACTIVITY: eBay channel next to the own shop). Identity and operator are clear, but the product titles are mixed: many 1930s-60s signs, pumps and WW2 items, but also 1970s-1999 items (Chi-Lites bus headsign, Goodwood 1999, Coca-Cola Light, Davanti tyres, a 1981 parachute), vehicles (1971 Morgan, 1956 Land Rover, Willys Jeep), own-brand merchandise (T-shirts, mugs) and many undated items, so a pre-1970 majority and the new-goods share cannot be confirmed from titles. Re-check with item pages.

Gutlin Clocks and Antiques (Kings Road, Chelsea; proprietors John and Mark Coxhead; Shopify): products.json holds 224 products of which 29 (13 percent) are newly made retail clocks listed under bare model codes (Lotscher-xxxx cuckoo and wall clocks with 1-day or 8-day movements, QUARTZ-xxxx 'Cuckoolino' quartz cuckoo clocks, GBP 81 to 1,308). The stock also includes about 35 Jaeger-LeCoultre Atmos clocks of which more than half are 1970s to 1991 and several are described as brand new condition, plus a repair-service product. New goods far above the 5 percent limit, alongside genuine 18th and 19th century clocks.

Ipplepen Interiors (Devon, Shopify; antique, vintage and retro furniture restored in its own workshop): the stock is mostly genuine antique and vintage furniture (110 items available, about 100 itemised with prices), but the public shop has a dedicated 'Digital Art' collection of 10 NFT digital artworks (A101 to A110, GBP 199 each, product type NFT), about 9 percent of the available items, plus 'Reprodux' and 'reproduction' pieces and many 1960s and 1970s 'retro' teak items. A dedicated new digital-art section above the 5 percent limit under the no-mix rule; the antique furniture part would otherwise qualify, so this deserves a re-look if the section is removed.

Jennings & Cox (Shopify): 63 products, 39 available; about a third of the available items are newly made decor (handmade fabric 'Country House Bow' hanging bows, product type Country House Bow, GBP 25 to 70, and hand-painted terracotta bowls), alongside Victorian and antique pine furniture, paintings and Italian Florentine trays. New goods far above 5 percent.

Marmorea London (WooCommerce, Store API total 538 products, prices mostly on request): besides antique fireplaces (121), antique mirrors, lighting and objects the catalogue holds a Wood Flooring range of 51 new product lines (e.g. 'Cabin Oak Black', 'Stone Aged Smoked Natural', 'Tudor Oak Cognac', herringbone and Versailles oak panels) and 22 'Reproduction Fireplaces' (new marble surrounds), about 14 percent new goods; a further 212 items sit under 'Circa: 20th Century Design' with many 1970s to 1990s designer pieces and a faux bronze Louvre bust reproduction.

Norfolk Antique & Reclamation Centre (Panxworth, company number 09655462, appointment-only yard): a reclamation and architectural salvage centre whose stock tree is dominated by building materials (bricks including a 'New Bricks' category, roofing, paving, flooring, windows, sanitaryware, radiators, doors) with an Antiques department as one of about 20 top-level categories. Reclamation merchant, not a predominantly antique or vintage dealer, and new bricks are sold.

Furniture Chapter (Budleigh Salterton, Devon; Weebly shop; Unit 6 Salterton Workshops EX9 6RJ, tel 07817 984505): a tiny itemised stock of about 28 antique and vintage pieces with prices (e.g. Regency rosewood set of 6 chairs GBP 1,500, Victorian mahogany tripod table GBP 295), but the footer reads 2016 and the Weebly sitemap shows every page, including the product pages, last published 2021-07-21 and 2022-10-03, so there is no evidence the stock is current. No imprint operator beyond the trading name. Re-check whether the site is updated.

Non-vintage lines: boxed Swarovski figurines (about 174 product URLs, 9%, annual editions 1989-2006) and Deagostini build kits (about 62, 3%). Estimated about 85% of listings are antique or vintage before 1970. Borderline identity: the About page calls itself a collector offering 'spare items from our own collection' ('Unlike traders') while running a full webshop with terms, sold archive and an eBay store link; terms state 'Www.uniqueitemsgb.co.uk is owned and operated by UniqueItemsGB' with no legal entity or named person. Contact: +44 7515821240, info@uniqueitemsgb.co.uk, location 'Wolseley Road, CR44JQ London, England'; delivery page offers 'FREE pick up collection from CR44JQ London possible' and the About page says 'We're based in London and ship worldwide'. Items are sourced from fairs, auctions and house clearances (purchasing only); the site sells at fixed prices, no own auctions seen. No contemporary art.

Second storefront of Devonshire Fine Art, 9 Church Street, Modbury, Devon PL21 0QW (same operator, address and telephone 01548 830872 as the ADDED antique-maps-online.co.uk; handoff candidate). Core stock is genuine antique: roughly 1,300 itemised Vanity Fair prints, 16th-19th century engravings and original early-20th-century watercolour caricatures with maker, date and price (e.g. Spy Vanity Fair caricature 'Mr. Winston Leonard Spencer Churchill' 27 Sep 1900 GBP 1,650; Sir Joseph Chitty watercolour 1885 GBP 2,995); the FAQ states 'we never sell modern reproductions'. HOWEVER the main menu carries a dedicated section 'Original Caricatures - Norman Hood Sporting Caricatures' with 18 sub-pages (England/Wales cricket and rugby legends, motor sport, darts, tennis, golf, football) holding about 218 newly made original caricatures of current and recent sports personalities (Joe Root, Jos Buttler, Lewis Hamilton, Alun Wyn Jones, Shane Williams) priced GBP 85-125 each; the artist Norman Hood is a living cartoonist with his own studio (career from the late 1960s, features on BBC and Sky Sports). That is about 14 percent of the roughly 1,550 priced items and about a quarter of all catalogue pages: a dedicated new contemporary-artwork section far above the 5 percent limit of the 2026-11-26 no-new-goods-mix rule (the operator's other site antique-fine-art.com was excluded NEW_GOODS_MIX for the same reason). Auction check: no auctions on the site. Borderline note for the owner: everything outside the Norman Hood section qualifies and the owner Party Devonshire Fine Art stays live through antique-maps-online.co.uk; a handoff row can be added later if original caricatures by a living artist are accepted as a minor side line.

Paul Mitchell Ltd (17 Avery Row, London) is a picture-framing and frame-appraisal service: it supplies antique frames from an inventory and commissions high-quality handmade replica frames and a mirror-frame collection. The 'Our antique frames' page shows only example images by period without item listings or prices; no itemised, purchasable stock. Framing service with new replica frames, not an antiques dealer with an inspectable catalogue.

Payne & Son, Oxford jeweller and silversmith: the shop navigation is organised around new jewellery (wedding, engagement, gemstone and designer rings, WOLF jewellery boxes) and a designer list of living makers (Sheila Fleet, Kit Heath, Annie Ruthven-Taggart, Georg Jensen silverware designers and others), with secondhand and vintage jewellery as only one section. New-goods retail dominates.

Kent Antiques Limited (privacy policy names the company as data controller; phone 020 737 029 14; email info@kentantiques.com) is a London gallery of Islamic and Indian art (13th to 19th century) and Orientalist paintings, with itemised works on category pages (metalwork 11, Orientalist paintings 10 by named 19th-century artists, and a 5-item Modern & Contemporary Paintings category). Deferred because no street address is published on any page that could be read (contact page only gives the email form) and the category and portfolio pages return HTTP 403 to the ordinary client and renders only intermittently (ceramics, calligraphy, textiles never loaded), so the full catalogue and the contemporary share could not be measured.

Historic pre-1970 collectable coins are a minority of the catalogue, so the stock is not predominantly antique or vintage.

Paul Dawson Coins, The Shambles, York (Shopify): the products feed lists 222 products: 95 coins, 55 fossils, 28 bank notes, 24 medals and militaria, 13 miscellaneous and 4 artefacts. The miscellaneous section holds newly made goods such as gold-plated QEII and Diana commemorative coins and obsidian Egyptian-style figurines (13 items, about 6 percent, above the trivial limit), alongside 55 fossil specimens (25 percent natural history, not antiques) and 23 coins with dates from 1970 onward. Mixed new goods and non-antique stock.

markhill.net redirects (301) to https://markhillpublishing.com/ (Mark Hill, antiques broadcaster and author; WooCommerce shop). The shop is organised around his own newly published books (Fat Lava, Hi Sklo Lo Sklo, Caithness Glass, Alla Moda and a new hardback, sold in a dedicated Books category) and paid services (valuations, lectures), next to a smaller stock of vintage glass, ceramics and prints (mostly shown as sold, plus a free e-catalogue of 20 objects). The living-artist share is far above the trivial limit for an antique dealer.

Newly made contemporary objects in a dedicated section make it a vintage and new mix beyond the trivial limit (about 6 of an estimated 80 or more listed pieces).

decision.basis: Absolutely Nice Vintage (Carlisle, Cumbria; Shopify; est. 2013 by Damian and Mark) is an own-stock curator of '20th century furniture, homeware, objects and art work' with a very large catalogue (products.json: 1,250 products, 299 available, newest 2026-11-19): Danish and British mid-century teak, G Plan, Ercol, Anglepoise, mirrors, lamps, filing cabinets, books and art. Qualification hinges on the pre-1970 share, which cannot be established with confidence: of about 165 titles that state a decade, 1950s 33, 1960s 63, 1930s-1940s 10, but 1970s 39, 1980s 16 and 1990s 4 (about 36% from 1970 onward), while most of the remaining titles are undated 'Vintage' items (frameless mirrors, metal filing cabinets, lamps, Vintage IKEA pieces, 1980s Robin Day) whose age is unknown. Also present and small: about 25 contemporary-labelled items (Contemporary Original abstract paintings, Nemo chair, Alessi cutlery, IKEA mirror, about 2%), a self-published photobook and a Carlisle bauble (new goods, trivial). Majority-vintage cannot be shown above 0.95 confidence; owner/orchestrator to decide whether a mid-century (1950s-70s) catalogue qualifies. Contact data were not collected because the dealer is not being onboarded.

Jenny Wood Antiques (50A Upper Tything, Worcester) is a bricks-and-mortar antique shop. The site (WordPress) has only Home/Buying/Selling/About/Contact pages; Selling Antiques page states that stock is constantly changing and visitors should visit the shop to view current items. No online catalogue or itemised stock with items/prices exists (checked home, selling-antiques, contact).

Johnson Antiques is a unit in the Levenshulme Antiques Village, Manchester (Wix site, no imprint with a legal operator, no published email, tel 07971 673176). The only online shop mentioned is a link to an eBay store (marketplace, not fetchable: HTTP 403). No inspectable itemised stock on the own site.

decision.basis: Stable Antiques, 46 West Street, Storrington, West Sussex, is an antiques centre run by Ian and Laura Wadey with 34 stallholders on two floors (antiques, furniture, bric-a-brac, house clearances, garden plants and statuary). The WordPress site has only Home, Next, Find us and Enquiry pages; there is no online catalogue or itemised stock, and the stock belongs to multiple stallholders rather than a single own-stock dealer.

Suffolk House Antiques (Andrew Singleton, established 1991) sells itemised early oak, country furniture, works of art and delftware, e.g. A George III burr ash cricket table circa 1780, A 16th century Nuremberg alms dish, a Christmas Selling Exhibition 2026 catalogue of 60+ pieces (not an auction: items for sale now, payment by BACS/cheque/cash); stock clearly qualifies, prices are not shown on the pages read (policy D acceptable). However the gallery in Yoxford was closed in May 2024 and the site publishes no postal, premises or correspondence address and no company/legal operator, only the header locality Yoxford, Suffolk. Sunbury and Sandown Antiques Market is run by Surrey Antiques Ltd (company number 10943281, PO Box 155, Shepperton TW17 9WE): an organiser of recurring outdoor and indoor antiques markets (Kempton, Sandown, Wimbledon, Denbies) where independent stallholders sell. The site lists market dates, stall bookings and admission only; it holds no online catalogue and sells no own stock.

The Antiques Centre York (The Antiques Centre York Ltd, Allenby House, 41 Stonegate, York YO1 8AW; Shopify site) is a full-service antiques centre: its About page states that all antiques, jewellery and collectables in-store and online do not belong to the centre but to a community of over 120 dealers who rent units; dealers page recruits further dealers and the centre settles sales to them. Online stock (thousands of items, collections such as Royal Doulton, Beswick, Lladro, Border Fine Arts, costume jewellery, gifts under GBP x) therefore belongs to many independent dealers, and a large part is post-1970 ceramics and collectables; this is a multi-dealer centre/marketplace rather than a single dealer selling its own stock. products.json is behind a bot challenge and was not bypassed.

decision.basis: Trecastle Antiques Centre (Old School building, Trecastle, LD3 8UP, A40) is a bricks-and-mortar antiques centre with a general mix (furniture, glassware, tools, pinball machines, signs, militaria, jewellery, clothing, garden ornaments, LPs). The Wix site has only a home page and a Gallery page described as a small selection of items for sale (photographs without item titles, descriptions or prices); there is no itemised online catalogue, and the centre format with no named single operator indicates multiple stock owners.

Val's Collectables (WooCommerce, Isle of Wight; 176 products via the public store API) sells second-hand silver and gemstone jewellery labelled antique and vintage. First 100 products read: most are generic 925 silver pendants, rings, necklaces and chains with no stated period or with 1970s-era hallmarks (Birmingham 1975, London 1979), many branded modern pieces (Thomas Sabo, Tiffany Return to Tiffany bracelet, Butler and Wilson tennis bracelet, a ring New in box), plus a few genuinely older items (antique 800 silver gilt filigree brooches, c1960s artisan ring). Estimated share of pre-1970 items well under half; used modern jewellery does not qualify (policy C).

Vincent's Motorcycles and Antiques (Weebly, Isle of Wight) is primarily a used motorcycle, scooter and car dealer (home page lists engine-size categories, project vehicles, parts, a Yamaha XJ900 2003, a Jaguar XJ 2001, a BSA A65 1967 priced as a restored bike; delivery to the Portsmouth ferry) with side sections for motor memorabilia, records, toys, hobbies and curiosities. Used vehicles and general second-hand goods, not predominantly antique stock; no qualified antique catalogue.

Vintage Hereford (WooCommerce, 79 products via the public store API; email vintagehereford@gmail.com, no phone) sells a general mix: 19th-century brass, Russian silver and enamel, a Wainscot armchair, but also many undated Vintage USSR Lomonosov/Gzhel porcelain figurines, 1970s liquor bottles, a 1980s brass lamp and 1992 Vostok watches; only about a quarter of titles state a pre-1970 date, so a pre-1970 majority cannot be established. The site publishes no operator name, no postal address (collection only from the HR2 postcode area) and no imprint, so no location or operator can be asserted above 0.95. Deferred until identity, address and stock age mix can be confirmed.

Vintage White Antiques (Shopify; 1,207 products, 837 available via the public products.json) is dominated by vintage sewing patterns: 606 of the 837 available items. Of the 493 patterns whose title or description states a decade, only about 36 percent (177) date from the 1920s-1960s and about 64 percent (316) from the 1970s-1990s; a further 113 are undated modern-era commercial patterns (New Look, Vogue, Butterick). Together with the remaining mostly antique/vintage non-pattern items (sewing machines, transferware, enamel signs, packaging, kitchenalia) the estimated pre-1970 share is about 40-50 percent, i.e. not a majority, and 1970s-onward nostalgia does not qualify (policy C). The site also publishes no operator name or postal address (contact form only; free collection at antiques fairs).

Warehouse701 (Hereford, historic WW1 warehouse; furniture, reclamation and homewares) sells reclaimed architectural salvage and furniture but the site navigation shows a large new-goods retail part: Homewares and Gifts with branded new suppliers (Keith Brymer Jones, Annie Sloan, Fusion Paints, Little Greene Paints, Aquarelle Home, Ashwood Leather, Pachamama, By Royale, Forever England, Bio Farm Trading, Ellumiere), a New Building Supplies section, new paints, garden structures and planters, and a Group A parcel delivery scheme for selected homewares and hardware. Dedicated new-goods sections far exceed the 5 percent tolerance; the business is a general reclamation yard and homewares retailer rather than an antiques dealer.

WeBuyVintage (trading name of The Antiques Collective Ltd, company number 14385719, registered office 20-22 Wenlock Road, London N1 7GU, per its terms) is a buying business: roadshows, home visits and in-store purchases of gold, jewellery, coins, watches and collectables for same-day payment offers. The home page (about 3.3 MB, read via bounded curl after the fetcher limit) menu holds About Us, Items We Buy, Roadshows, Home Visits, Sell In-Store, Reviews, FAQs and Contact; no shop or itemised stock for sale is offered online.

decision.basis: Carlos Garcia Interiors (London and Norfolk) is an interior design practice. The About page says its shop catalogue is a newly launched 'collection of fabrics and wallpapers, based on original documents' and a 'collection of furniture derived from antiques pieces and respectfully adapted to modern living'; the home page items are new products (Rectory Rose on Glazed Linen, Wolterton Grand Sofa, Jajim fabric). New-goods retail by a designer with no antique stock; not an antiques dealer.

Catharine Miller Gallery, 12 Hollywood Road, Chelsea: 'Contemporary Art Gallery' (page title); the About page says 'Paintings, prints and sculpture from 1950 to the present day', and the catalogue is organised as Contemporary Artists, Mid-Century Modern, Sculpture and Ceramics, with 502 items under New to the Gallery and 588 under Mid-Century Modern. Stock is mainly post-1950 and contemporary works.

Fisher London (7 Rugby Street, Bloomsbury; BADA member) is a genuine antiques shop, but the website has no itemised catalogue: the Gallery page shows nine category pictures (Ceramics, Silver, Treen, Paintings, Metalware, Antiquities, Furniture, Ethnographic, Glass) with no item titles, descriptions or prices, and the other pages are Diary, Instagram, Press, Testimonials, About and Contact. No product pages exist to inspect.

French Affair Antiques & Interiors, Sheffield (Unit 2 Montrose Works, open by appointment). The About page says 'whilst most of our stock is antique or vintage we also stock a variety of new lights and homeware', and the catalogue has a dedicated 'Bespoke' category (Occasional/Dining/Kitchen Table, Pair of Coffee Tables) and many newly made items: French Style Farmhouse Table and French Style Dining Table ('reclaimed pine top, painted base', 'can be custom made to your dimensions'), French Empire style chandelier wired to modern UK standard, handmade Moroccan cactus silk runner (new textile), shaker style hooks. Several listings per category are new or made-to-order, well above the 5 percent limit.

French Mirror House (Headcorn, Kent): about half of the 62 product pages are antique 18th/19th-century French and Italian mirrors, but the other half sits in 'Revived furniture' and 'Bespoke furniture' sections of pieces re-created by the shop: 'Textured Artisan Chest of Drawers - Functional Art, Handmade, individually created by French Mirror House using my signature heavy plaster technique', 'Decorative Wooden Keepsake Box - hand-painted by French Mirror House', hand-painted and stencilled chests of drawers sold as made-to-order commissions ('a similar green diamond chest can be created', 'Bespoke Commission Antique Sage Green Diamond Tallboy', 'hand painted commission' for a customer). These newly finished and made-to-order decorative pieces form a dedicated section far above 5 percent of the catalogue.

Georgia Lacey Antiques (Bodiam, East Sussex, by appointment) sells Swedish painted antiques but the catalogue is split into Current Stock, 'Luxe Editions' ('the world's finest luxury Gustavian reproduction furniture hand crafted to order in England', Freja oak console GBP 8,250 ex VAT, Stockholm bedside chests) and 'Bespoke Gustavian Furniture' ('handmade to order in Stockholm'); the contact page says 'We also have reproduction hand made Gustavian furniture'. Current Stock also lists new decor (Organic Portuguese vase, aqua green glass vase, black melange pots, tall glass vase) and an abstract painting by a contemporary artist. Dedicated reproduction/new-goods sections, far above the 5 percent limit.

Britton at War (Mr S Britton, 18 Francis Sheldon Crt, Peninsula Rd, Winchester SO22 4FB; militaria dealer attending fairs). The stock would qualify: 1,522 items in 'All available items as listed' (WWI/WWII British and Commonwealth militaria, about 90 percent before 1970), fixed prices (e.g. officers Royal Gloucestershire Militia shako GBP 650, WWII RAF MkVII flying goggles GBP 450). But current activity cannot be confirmed: the Shows & Events page lists only 2019 fairs, Latest News is empty, the newest item images that load were uploaded in Dec 2023 (product 12977 on 2023-12-25, 12969 on 2023-12-23), and the 28 newest listings (12978-13005) have no retrievable image file (HTTP 404 on their catalogue and main images). Recheck for dated listings or confirmed trading.

Chapter II Fine Living (Jonny Stenson and Louisa Kennedy; 25 Queslett Road East, Streetly, Sutton Coldfield B74 2ER, open Tuesday to Sunday 10-4 per the contact page). The stock style would qualify (architectural and decorative antiques and vintage: Edwardian plaster putti GBP 480, vintage Fornasetti tray GBP 795, Brucciani plaster statue GBP 1,795, Hardman and Co window GBP 2,495; about 70 percent of a 42-title sample is pre-1970). But the catalogue is dormant: only 4 items are unsold (home page 'Latest Stock'), 160 of the 164 product pages are in the Sold archive, those 4 item images were uploaded in March and April 2024 and the blog's last posts are 2022-2023. Current trading and stock cannot be confirmed. Domain chaptertwoantiques.co.uk redirects (301) to this host.

Decided together with that domain; no separate source.

Dear Old Blighty (militaria shop run by Bernard Pass per the About page and image-copyright line; 7,679 items in All Items, WW1/WW2 collectables) looks like a second storefront of the already ADDED operator Coldstream Military Antiques, Marlow (live Party pty_01m8cwgq89efgt4tpx8k3r1bsv, listing source ls_01m8cwgq8ae3j8dw517g3jhdab, ledger GB): both sites give the same telephone +44 (0)1628 488 188, the same wording 'is an internet shop only, based in Marlow Buckinghamshire. We are sorry we do not have any viewing or collection facilities', and the Dear Old Blighty About page lists coldstreammilitaryantiques.com among its 'sister sites' (with buywyze.com, regimentalbadges.com, regimentalbrooches.com, sallyslbadges.com). The two sites name different people (Steven Bosley founded Coldstream in 1978; Bernard Pass is named here) and publish no company name, so common ownership cannot be proven from first-party pages: orchestrator handoff to decide whether this is the existingOperator flow or a separate operator. Separate own catalogue (Dear Old Blighty uses its own ph9 shop and postage terms). Activity also uncertain: a despatch notice of 2025-08-28 says it 'will be taking a Break From Militaria Zone' and the newest listed item image was uploaded 2025-02-16. Stock qualifies (original WW1/WW2 militaria, no auctions or new goods seen).

French Farmhouse Furniture (Bristol workshops; imports unrestored French and Italian antique beds, armoires, commodes). The site holds 647 product pages but 622 are in the Sold archive and the Stock ('Shop home') category and the Latest Items list show no unsold item; the About page says 'Our main antiques showroom of current stock is now in Lorfords, Hanger 1, Babdown Airfield, nr Tetbury' (lorfordsantiques.com, 01666 505111), so the website no longer lists current own stock. Contact page gives only info@frenchfarmhousefurniture.co.uk (no phone, no address). Stock type (18th/19th-century French and Italian antiques) would qualify. Recheck for new current listings.

Henry Nicholls Antiques (ph9 antiques shop, 290 catalogue pages incl. sold, 36 current items such as an 18th Century Bracket Clock by Thomas Wagstaffe GBP 2,450, an Early Victorian Memorial Ring GBP 595, a Meissen plate GBP 95, Georg Jensen and Victorian silver and jewellery) sells genuinely antique stock with prices, no auctions or new goods seen, and publishes a phone (07866 436 371 / 0782 590 9216) and email (ask@henrynichollsantiques.co.uk). However no postal address, premises or correspondence address is published on the contact, about, terms, privacy or blog pages (the about page only says the founder 'opened up a shop in sunny Worthing' nearly 30 years ago and a fraud alert mentions cold callers in Worthing; neither states the current base). The page titles name 'Henry Nicholls Antiques Ltd' but Companies House lists company 07731204 as HENRY NICHOLLS & SON ANTIQUES LTD (formerly Henry Nicholls Antiques Limited) with an accountancy registered office in London, so the exact current legal operator is not confirmed by first-party text either. No location or operator can be asserted above 0.95; defer until an address and legal operator are published.

Justin Manley Art & Antiques (ph9 shop, 129 catalogue pages incl. sold: 102 art, 10 lighting, 10 decorative items, 7 furniture; Scandinavian paintings by artists such as Nils Rosberg 1865-1957, Alfred Hedlund 1884-1930, Svante Kede 1877-1955, Swedish glass by Orrefors and Kosta, 1950s teak lamps) states 'Pieces mostly by recognised Artists and Designers of the 20th Century'. Contact page gives phone +44 (0)7854 40 42 22 and email manley.j@hotmail.co.uk but no premises or address: only 'I now live in the West Midlands so can deliver pieces for viewing in this area', by appointment. No operator name beyond the trading name and no address or town is published, so no location can be asserted above 0.95. The stock age mix is also unresolved: a noticeable share of the paintings are by artists active after 1945 (for example Lennart Frisk 1943-2000, Arnold Lindblom b.1930, Miklos Nemeth 1934-2012, a Danish 'contemporary artist'), which would have to be measured against the pre-1945 modern-art rule before any onboarding. Defer until a location is published.

Katharine Pole Antique Textiles (ph9 shop, 1,235 catalogue pages incl. sold: 583 textiles, 318 cushions, 191 decorative objects, 87 vintage costume, 42 furniture, 14 greetings cards). Antique French textiles are genuine, but the catalogue holds two new-goods parts: a dedicated Greetings Cards category (14 newly printed cards of antique textile details, GBP 2.75 each, 'printed on 300gsm silk card ... with envelope and cellophane bag') and a Cushions category of 318 newly made-up cushions (about 26 percent of the catalogue; for example 'Fez Silk Embroidered Cushion Morocco 19th Century' GBP 550: antique embroidery on a slip-stitched cover with a duck-feather pad). A dedicated new-goods section and more than 5 percent made-up goods fall under the no vintage/new mixes rule. Contact: info@katharinepole.com, 0774 761 6692, showroom in London by appointment (no address).

Milos Antiques (ph9 shop of antique and mid-century furniture, lighting, mirrors and decorative items, 767 catalogue pages incl. sold; about page: 'traditional and contemporary objects from 1970 back to the 19th century', sourced by 'Robbie') publishes a mobile (+44 (0)787 668 4588) and email (robbie@milosantiques.co.uk) but no address at all: the contact page says only 'Please contact us for full address details and to make an appointment', and no town, company name or imprint appears on the home, about, contact, terms or privacy pages. No location or legal operator can be asserted; the stock age mix (mid-century and 1970 pieces alongside antiques) is also unmeasured. Defer until an address and operator are published.

Mimi Roberts is an artist who sells her own current still-life oil paintings (about the site: 'Mimi Roberts is an artist who specialises in still life painting ... the subject of her work is taken from life', commissions accepted, new paintings shown at the Battersea fair) alongside 20th-century glass. The sitemap lists 2,038 catalogue pages of which 1,245 (about 61 percent) are her own paintings (titles such as Broccoli GBP 350, Bowl of quinces GBP 600, Fennel GBP 350) and 793 are 20th-century glass vases; an artist selling her own current work as the majority of the catalogue is a contemporary-art business under the owner decision of 2026-11-24. Contact: mimi@mimiroberts.co.uk, 01608 686886, by appointment only.

Nude not Rude (trading name of Big Sky Fine Art Limited, VAT GB384240107; Companies House 07145992) is a themed gallery of original figurative art, 34 catalogue pages in total, described as 'original art from the eighteenth to twentieth centuries'. Reading all 34 titles: about 19 are clearly pre-1945 (1819-1860s academic studies, 1895 school drawing, 1930s French oils, 1937, 1944 Devas), but about 9 are clearly post-1945 (1950s watercolour, 1967 drawings, c.1965 Cornish oil, 1967 Frink bronze maquette, 1975 Venetian nude, 1980s watercolour, 1990s oil by a Cardiff artist, a 2003 mixed-media work) and about 6 more are undated mid- or late-20th-century pieces, so the stock is not predominantly pre-1945 and the contemporary share (about 13 percent) is well above the 5 percent allowed. The only location given is 'the Jurassic coastline of Dorset', viewing by appointment (phone +44 (0)1305 581426, art@bigskyfineart.com). Excluded under the post-war and modern art rule.

Odyssey Fine Arts (Odyssey Fine Arts Ltd., 129 Lisson Grove, Marylebone, London NW1 6UP; phone +44 (0)20 7730 9942; odysseyfinearts@aol.com; Companies House 02832853 active with the same address) is a small ph9 shop of antique engravings, drawings and Art Deco prints: 28 catalogue pages, 21 of them on the Sold page, 7 currently for sale and all genuinely old (Roman Emperors woodcuts 1559 POA, Chinese pith paper paintings c.1850 GBP 3,900, Thomas Moore Ferns of Great Britain 1855 POA, Benedictus Relais pochoirs 1930 GBP 3,600, Bloch fish engravings 18th century GBP 290 each, an Arts & Crafts table c.1910, Laure Albin Guillot 1945). No auctions, no new goods, no contemporary art for sale (sold archive includes 1971-73 prints and a c.1980 chair). However the home page still announces 'the Autumn Fair 1st - 6th October 2019' and no dated content after that is visible, so current trading cannot be confirmed from first-party pages. Defer and re-check that the shop is still active.

Penny Worrall (ph9 shop, VAT 398 5669 16, studio in Purley, Surrey, penny@pennyworrall.com, +44 (0)7795 343 042) sells newly made home furnishings: of 2,134 catalogue pages, 1,584 are 'vintage textile cushions' (cushions and lampshades newly made up from vintage woven textiles, 'I like to find uses for these textiles ... by making them into cushions and lampshades'), 310 are 'contemporary handwoven textile cushions', 86 are mini lavender pillows, plus lampshades, lamps and framed textiles. Cushion and lampshade production with new pads and contemporary handwoven cushions is a new-goods business, not an antiques or vintage dealer (the genuine vintage items are only a handful of blankets, quilts and decorative pieces).

Rutland Garden Classics (Chris Hamilton proprietor, Pillings Rd, Oakham LE15 6QF; info@rutlandgardenclassics.co.uk, 01572 720070) sells garden ornaments and planters, 362 catalogue pages. Besides reclaimed items it has dedicated new-goods sections: Corten Steel Planters & Sculptures (new rusty-steel planters from GBP 145, fire pits, 'Rusty Love Hearts' sculptures), a Bronze Sculpture section of 80 items (newly cast bronze hares, stags and dogs, many 'inc free delivery'), Stainless steel sculpture, Philip Simmonds Sculptural Ceramics (contemporary ceramics), teak garden benches, terracotta pots and olive jars, plus a Black Friday sale. Dedicated new-goods sections far above 5 percent of the catalogue, so a garden-ware retailer rather than a predominantly antique dealer.

Scout Decorative (ph9 shop, 607 catalogue pages incl. sold: 'The Collection' 201 and 'The Cornish Collection' 195, mostly 20th-century drawings, abstract and figurative art by named mid-century and later artists, plus 92 decorative objects, 60 chairs, 24 furniture, 24 outdoor items and rugs, some clearly antique such as an early 19th-century circular table and 19th-century Puglian pots) publishes only a phone (+44 (0)790 365 2469) and a gmail address (scoutdecorative@gmail.com): there is no about, address, town, operator or terms text anywhere on the site. No location or operator can be asserted, and the share of post-1945 and contemporary art in the two collections (for example 'contemporary abstract Welsh landscape', 'Ivan Bray abstract acrylic on board', 'late 20th century stone sculpture') is unmeasured and looks substantial, so even with an address the dealer would need a stock review. Defer.

Sevenoaks Fine Art Ltd (gallery of 19th and 20th century British and French paintings, 343 catalogue pages incl. sold, also listed on 1stDibs) has no usable published contact: the Contact pages (page_102 to 104) still carry the ph9 template placeholders ('1 Your Address, Your Town', '+44 (0)1234 567 890', 'youremail@youremail.com'), and the About page only says 'please do send us an email'. The privacy policy gives a postal address (2 Randall Hill Road, Wrotham, Sevenoaks TN15 7BN) but neither an email nor a phone number appears anywhere, so no contact fact can be asserted and the dealer cannot be onboarded. The stock is also a modern-art mix to be measured before any onboarding: artists such as Maurice Loirand 1922-2008, Adrianus van Noort 1914-2003, Noelle Verheggen 1929-2017, Robert Farquhar b.1937, Keith Dunkley b.1942 and Geoffrey Chatten b.1938 appear next to 19th-century and pre-1945 works. Defer until a real email or phone is published.
