Every page of lorfordsantiques.com tried (home, sitemap.xml, contact-us, about-us, http and https; only robots.txt answers) returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare managed challenge ('Just a moment...') to the generic fetcher, plain curl with an ordinary browser User-Agent and one ordinary headless Chromium render; no challenge bypass was attempted, so no first-party page could be read. Third-party search results only (leads, not evidence): Lorford's Antiques Limited (Companies House 05500386), main showroom at 30 Long Street, Tetbury GL8 8AQ with own stock, a second site in a former RAF hangar at Babdown housing a dealer collective (reports of 19 to 52 dealers) and a sister line Lorfords Contemporary (new handmade furniture), which would indicate a multi-dealer and new-goods mix; this cannot be confirmed or excluded from first-party pages. Re-check when the site is readable.

Bayfield Hall Antiques and Interiors (Bayfield Hall, Holt, Norfolk NR25 7JN, 01263 715538) is an antiques centre in the Old Stables 'home to several very individual traders': the Our Dealers page lists M. D. Cannell Antiques and Norfolk Rugs, Jane Cave (Deco Cave), Norfolk Antiques, Interior Deli (scented candles, photo frames, quirky interior gifts, new goods) and Marilyn Bookal Antiques, each with its own phone and email. The WordPress site has no itemised catalogue or shop (only an Instagram feed, events and directions), so it is a multi-dealer centre without inspectable stock of its own. The individual dealers are separate leads.

Alice Through The Looking Glass (14 Cecil Court, London WC2N 4HE; Shopify): the shop's own product list (47 products) has 18 'Books & Collectables' (antique and rare Alice editions and some new titles such as the owner's own 'Through a Looking Glass Darkly' at GBP 19.95/70), but also dedicated sections for newly made goods: 'Art' (8 current art prints, e.g. 'The Cheshire Cat - Monochrome Art Print' GBP 15, 'Limited Edition Fine Art Print' GBP 75), 'Cards, Confectionery & Ceramics' (8, e.g. tote bag GBP 24, espresso cup GBP 27.50, chocolate gift box GBP 16), 'T-Shirt' (4 branded t-shirts GBP 15-20) and a 'Gifts, Cards & Note Books' menu section. Roughly 20 of 47 listings are new goods, far above the 5 percent tolerance, so the shop is a vintage/new mix. No auctions seen.

Antique-knives.co.uk (Dave Watson Solutions Ltd, Farnham Common, Bucks; Concept500 shop): the shop lists 18 items in total and every available item is a book: newly published reference books of the operator's own publishing line (e.g. 'Viking Era Swords' GBP 75, 'Gothic to Medieval Swords and Helmets 1000 to 1550AD' published April 2022, 'Antique Fishing Priests' GBP 25, 'The Art of Eastern Australia' GBP 85) plus a few used knife reference books. The categories 'Arms and Armour' and 'Fishing Books' hold only books; the 'Knives & daggers - Bowie knives' category is empty (0 items) and the only other entry is a 'WANTED' notice. No antique knives or arms are currently offered, so the current stock is new/used books rather than antiques. No auctions seen.

John Wilson Antiques (antique firearms and edged weapons, sole trader, phone 07941 477043): the site describes itself as 'currently a gallery of a small selection of items rather than an active sales site - if there is anything that catches your eye then please contact me to check availability'. The four category pages (Flintlocks, Percussion, Obsolete calibre, Other items) show a handful of photographed items per page with prices or SOLD marks (e.g. 'Holster pistol by W.Bond GBP 1150'), there is no basket, no shop and no published postal address or location (copyright 2017), and fair dates are the only current content. A showcase gallery without a shop and without any address cannot be onboarded as an inspectable catalogue with a location.

Arabella Bianco (costume jewellery and accessories, 977 listings in view-all-products, 970 product URLs in the sitemap). The shop's own 'Era' filter shows Antique over 100 yrs 64, Vintage 20-100 yrs 804, Modern up to 20 yrs 83, New 19, i.e. 10.5 percent modern/new items. 'Vintage 20-100 years' reaches into the 1980s and 1990s, so it does not prove pre-1970: by title/URL 349 of 970 listings (36 percent) are dated or styled before 1970 (Art Deco, Art Nouveau, Victorian, 1930s-1960s), 165 (17 percent) are explicitly 1970s or later, and 456 are undated; a 40-item spread sample of the undated titles read on their own product pages gave 11 pre-1970 (28 percent), 10 dated 1970s-1990s, 5 modern/new and 14 undated. Estimated pre-1970 share is therefore about 49 percent (at most about 55 percent), not a clear majority, and modern/new pieces exceed the 5 percent tolerance. No auctions.

The Black Cat Bookshop (Leicester; PO Box 8662, Wigston LE18 9BB; blackcatuk@aol.com): the own website is a brochure page with three links, an eBay seller page, an AbeBooks search link ('search some of our books available online'), a fairs list and a contact page. No own catalogue or shop exists; the stock described (used and rare books from antiquarian to modern firsts, football programmes, comics) is offered only on eBay and AbeBooks. It also describes itself as selling second-hand and modern books, which would not be a majority antique in any case.

Bloomsbury Revisited is a small British company that makes and sells new lampshades, lamp bases, wallpapers and cushions inspired by the Bloomsbury artists ('All our products are made in the UK'; WooCommerce shop with categories Lampshades, Clip-On Lampshades, Wallpaper, Cushions, Bases, Hand Painted). The catalogue is entirely newly made goods, with no antique or vintage stock.

Bone Interiors (3 Market Square, Petworth GU28 0AH; sarah@boneinteriors.com, 01798 343283; Squarespace): the site is a shop window with an 'Our Story' text and a single 'Furniture' page that shows one featured item ('Charming Painted 4 Drawer Desk GBP 395', posted 24 March 2025). There is no itemised catalogue to inspect. The shop also describes itself as offering 'contemporary, classic and vintage furniture and accessories' including new goods such as Manuel Canovas candles and gifts, so the mix would in any case not be predominantly antique.

Books Written By (Northampton): a general bookshop whose own About page says 'we specialise in new, used and second hand titles along with rare, antiquarian and out of print books' and that it can order 'any title on demand' from the UK's largest wholesaler. The category tree is general (Cookery/Wine, Health/Beauty/Spirit, Crime, Fiction, Sci-Fi/Horror/Fantasy, Sport/Hobbies, Religion, Reference/Study) and the front-page titles are modern secondhand books (e.g. 'The Botanical Palette: Colour for the Botanical Painter', 'How (not) to Paint a Locomotive'). New books and modern second-hand books predominate; antiquarian items are a minor part.

Books by Nugget Box (Stafford; Extanium Book Seller shop): 'Specialists in Out of Print, Rare and Second Hand Books from Modern to Antiquarian'. About 1,300 itemised books (History 385, Fiction 220, Comics and Graphic Novels 122, Literature 89, Natural History 79, Photography 79, Ornithology 76, History of Companies 75, Children's 59, Waterways 44, Folio Publications 36, Audiobooks 9; the 'Antiquarian' category holds only 16). Publication dates read on 37 spread-sample item pages: 12 published before 1970 (32 percent), 25 from 1970 onward (up to 2022), so the stock is mostly used modern books.

Chilton Books (The Lodge, Newton Road, Sudbury CO10 2RS; Chrislands shop with 13,983 itemised books, specialising in theology, Bibles and prayer books, masonic and Suffolk books). Publication years read on eight author-sorted pages spread over the whole catalogue (160 items, 5 undated) plus the curated front page: 64 of 155 dated items published before 1970 (41 percent), 91 from 1970 on (including many 1990s pamphlets); with the front page included the share is 47 percent. Antiquarian Bibles are a minority within a mostly used modern religious catalogue, so the majority-antique test is not met.

C L Hawley (26 Belgrave Street, Skipton BD23 1QB; Extanium Book Seller shop): about 9,575 itemised second-hand books, of which 9,147 sit in the 'Books GBP 10 and under' / 'Books GBP 20 and under' bins (typical prices GBP 3-6, academic and literary paperbacks), only 67 are in 'Antiquarian', and the menu also has 'New Books' and 'Stationery'. Publication years read on a 103-item spread sample over both bins: 42 published before 1970 (41 percent) and 61 from 1970 on, so the catalogue is mostly used modern books.

Delph Books (Manchester; WooCommerce site): the 'Stock' page states 'You can search our current stock listings at AbeBooks.co.uk, AbeBooks.com and Biblio.com'. The own site has no book catalogue; its only shop items are two book-conservation products (Clearview dustwrapper protection film GBP 12 and GBP 14), which are new goods. The antiquarian and second-hand books are offered only on third-party marketplaces.

B Frank & Son, Newcastle (numismatists since 1983; phone 0191 413 8749; bfrankandson@aol.com; Yell website with an Ecwid store). The store is itemised and priced (British coins, World coins, tokens, banknotes, numismatic books) but the business also runs regular timed online auctions (own text: 'hold up to 12 online auctions every year'; the auctions page lists monthly MTS sales on EasyliveAuction.com and invites consignors: 'selling your collection ... through our online auctions'). First-party pages do not show whether the fixed-price store or the auction sales are the main business. Stock age is borderline as well: dated store items read on the rendered categories give British Coins 56 pre-1970 against 134 later (decimal coinage), World Coins 138 against 23, World Banknotes 20 against 5, with about 400 undated tokens/medallions and about 145 numismatic books (modern reference literature). Deferred rather than guessed: needs an owner view on the auction share and the age mix.

Bexley Medals and Militaria (proprietor R Larnder per 'Cheques payable to'; rick@bexleymedalsandmilitaria.co.uk, +44 (0)1322 523531; Concept500 shop). The itemised catalogue qualifies on its face (428 items in 23 categories: WW1, WW2 and Victorian-era medals, helmets, bayonets, swords, badges and uniforms, original period pieces; a few commission items; no auction) but the contact page gives the postal address only as 'Bexley Medals & Militaria, T.B.A., United Kingdom', the privacy and terms pages give no address, and the news page names only a fair venue (Hildenborough Village Hall). No business location can be recorded, so it cannot be onboarded until an address is published.

Black Hen Antiques & Decorative (sister and brother team 'based in West Sussex'; Shopify). The itemised catalogue qualifies (18 priced items in products.json, e.g. George III sterling silver marrow scoop GBP 145, framed 1805 and 1807 engravings GBP 95, Meiji bronze mirror GBP 85, Tudric pewter coffee pot c.1914 GBP 45; about 14 of 18 pre-1970, two post-1970 pieces and one contemporary watercolour) but the site publishes only an e-mail address (blackhenantiques@hotmail.com). There is no phone, no postal address, no operator name; the only place named is an outlet for gardenalia 'at Garden Sage Nurseries, near Hassocks, West Sussex'. Some featured items also show 'Sold out'. A county-level location and a gardenalia outlet do not establish a business location or stock location, so it is deferred until a fuller imprint is published.

J & SL Bonham, Antiquarian Booksellers (Flat 14, 84 Westbourne Terrace, London W2 6QE; ABA/ILAB/PBFA member per own text): an itemised static-HTML catalogue of rare travel, exploration, polar and mountaineering books with item numbers and prices (e.g. Alexander 'An Expedition of Discovery into the Interior of Africa' Colburn 1838 GBP 45; Andersson 'Lake Ngami' 1856 GBP 850), so the stock itself is antiquarian. However the home page still lists book fairs of June 2010, shows SSI template errors ('[an error occurred while processing this directive]'), gives a different e-mail (bonbooks@dial.pipex.com) than the order page (info@bonhambooks.co.uk), and the catalogue page headers show Last-Modified 31 March 2023. Current trading and the valid contact cannot be confirmed from first-party pages.

qualification.basis: London gallery of vintage sub-Saharan African textiles (Asante and Ewe kente, Yoruba adire and asooke, Fulani, Ivory Coast, Mali and Niger cloths), operated by Duncan Clarke (About page: PhD on Yoruba aso oke weaving), with a stall at F013 Alfies Antique Market, 13-25 Church Street, London NW8 8DT (Tuesday-Saturday 10am-5pm). WooCommerce store API lists 244 itemised products, each with its own page, photos, code and price, e.g. 'Wodaabe Horse Saddle Cloth, Niger' (circa 1970s, one in stock), 'Poli, Cameroun Indigo' (collected in the 1950s), 'Rare Lambswool Fulani Kaasa', 'Green and Blue on White' (Asante kente chiefs cloth circa 1930-1950). The site states 'All items on this site are vintage'. Age check on the product descriptions: 131 of 244 items state an age or period; 113 of those are before 1970 (kente chief cloths circa 1900-1950, adire eleko 1960s, indigo cloths 1920-1950s) and 18 are circa 1970 or later (up to circa 2000), i.e. 86 percent of dated items pre-1970; the other 113 are undated pieces sold as vintage. No auctions, no new goods, no contemporary art, no marketplace-only stock; catalogue far below 300,000.

No auctions (the word appears only in sourcing remarks such as 'sold in an auction in central Europe'), no contemporary art, not marketplace-only. Consignment selling for over fifty consignors and layaway are offered (fine under policy); a film and TV advisory and rental service is a side service. WooCommerce store API lists 296 itemised, priced products with photos (285 in stock), e.g. 'Antique Eustace brothers of Hale art nouveau copper tray' GBP 275, 'Pair of Danico pottery Art Nouveau / Skonvirke vases, Made in Denmark 1919-1929' GBP 499.99, 'Antique Minton blue cherub jug' GBP 59.99, 'Art Deco Part Tea set by Parrot and Co' GBP 65, 'Cenedese Scavo Murano vase' GBP 95. Age check on the full API list of 296 items from category tags and titles: only about 57 items (19 percent) sit exclusively in the 'Really Retro' / 1970s pottery and glass categories; the remainder are antique (1800-1915), 1920s-1940s or 1950s-1960s mid-century pieces, so well over half is pre-1970. No new goods (no reproduction or replica items found in names), no contemporary art, no marketplace-only stock; catalogue 296 listings. AUCTION SIDE ACTIVITY: none on the site; the eBay shop and antique-centre cabinet are side sales channels next to the own fixed-price webshop. No legal entity is named on the contact, terms or privacy pages, so the operator is recorded under the trading name.

omissions: no registered company name, company number, VAT number or proprietor is published; operator recorded under the trading name, the contact-page address is recorded as the business address only (online seller, no showroom claim)

shipping: only UK mainland free delivery (islands surcharged, rates not stated), worldwide delivery on request with weight-based airmail pricing and a dispatch-within-one-working-day statement are recorded; no rates for islands or foreign countries, no collection terms asserted
the Lotus Cottage Antique Centre cabinet in Long Melford and fair stalls are not recorded as locations (third-party venues, no address stated on the site)

decision.basis: Mangan Antiques (Saltham Barns, Runcton, Chichester; WooCommerce, 146 itemised products all at price on request) is mostly genuine antique and mid-century stock (19th-century furniture, Murano glass, Italian majolica, mirrors, chandeliers), but the shop has a dedicated 'Bespoke' category of 8 products (5.5 percent of the catalogue) that are newly made one-off pieces: lamps designed and built by John Mangan (verdigris lighthouse light, petrified-wood light, 'Girl resting on wood' lamp), a bespoke chandelier assembled from vintage Murano crystal, a church candlestick converted into a lamp with a new handmade shade, and Victorian boxes decoupaged and repainted by a contemporary artist. A dedicated made-to-order/new section above about 5 percent of items means NEW_GOODS_MIX under the 2026-11-26 no-mix rule; the dealer could be revisited if the Bespoke range is removed.

Antique Architectural Brass (proprietor Steven Vinall; Wix shop with itemised, priced period brass door furniture, lighting and fireplace accessories from the late 18th to mid 20th century, e.g. 'A late 19th Century urn shape knocker' GBP 275, 'An early Victorian rosewood library table' GBP 1,975; free tracked UK and worldwide postage on small to medium items) qualifies on stock, with phone 07968 286342 and email steven.vinall@hotmail.com. However the only address published is 'Lake District, UK' (a region, no town or street) plus a mention of selling through Hatchwell Antiques at the Furniture Cave on King's Road, Chelsea (a different trading name, no street number). No UK trading address of the operator is published, so it cannot be onboarded yet.

Antiques Central (owner Mark Ray, independent antiques and vintage dealer since 2017) runs a Squarespace store with itemised, priced antique and vintage small items (e.g. 'Fishing boats oil painting on canvas' circa 1912 GBP 95, Arts and Crafts copper jug, Japanese bronze jardiniere; prices include UK mainland postage, Royal Mail Tracked 48 / Parcelforce 48; no international orders; pickup by appointment). Stock appears to qualify and the e-mail info@antiquescentral.co.uk is published, but no business address is given anywhere (only 'Birmingham and Central England region' sourcing and a pick-up address that is confirmed after payment) and no phone number; the legal trading identity is only the trading name and owner name. No UK trading address is published, so it is deferred until one appears.

Orchestrator handoff: ukantiquesilver.com ('Wallis Antiques For Quality Silver', own catalogue of Georgian, Victorian and Art Deco antique silver and plate with category ranges 1702-2026, worldwide delivery by request-a-quote, built by ph9 web design) belongs to the operator that is already ADDED as newarkantiques.com: live Party pty_01m6f6vrvfeg9r62be5c4jrx3d 'Wallis Antiques' (source ls_01m6f6vrvtejyrjva4vmbh4f19, location ploc_01m6f6vs5wej5vbhjrnqr1f0np). Same business address on the contact page (Wallis Antiques, Kelham Road, Newark on Trent, Nottinghamshire NG24 1BX) as the existing location and the same phone 07871 245084 (+447871245084); the existing ledger row already records that phone and the Kelham Road NG24 1BX showroom. This is a separate own catalogue (different platform and domain), so it is a second storefront of an existing operator: no new Party is created here; it needs the existingOperator flow.

antiquesilver.uk answers HTTP 301 to https://www.ukantiquesilver.com/ (checked with curl). ukantiquesilver.com is the Wallis Antiques silver storefront recorded in this shard as a DEFERRED second storefront of the already ADDED operator (Party pty_01m6f6vrvfeg9r62be5c4jrx3d, newarkantiques.com), so this domain is a redirect alias and gets no source of its own.

Antiques and Jewellery (Wix template site, e-mail alan@antiquesandjewellery.com, phone 01526 351308): the 'Web Store' page renders empty (checked in headless Chromium), the home page shows only a handful of captioned photographs (e.g. '9ct Gold Edwardian bracelet') with no prices or item pages, and the contact page still carries the template placeholder '[your address here]'. No itemised stock and no published address or operator identity.

Antiqurio Militaria is a WooCommerce shop of authentic WW1/WW2 military antiques and ephemera (itemised and priced, e.g. 'WW2 German RZM Feldflasche 1939 dated' GBP 90; free UK shipping, worldwide by prior agreement) run by a collector with 40 years' experience; phone 07832 141303 is published in the header. It looks qualified on stock, but no trading address of any kind appears on the home, About, Contact, Shipping or Privacy pages (contact is a form only, no e-mail address is published and no operator name or company), so no UK trading address or e-mail can be recorded. The sister site legraantiques.co.uk (same phone 07832 141303; taxidermy, furniture, salvage) is queued as a lead.

geography.addressText: Apeman Interiors, Nunnington Studios, Low Farm, York YO62 5UR, United Kingdom

qualification.basis: Antiques store in Nunnington, North Yorkshire (About page: founded 2016 by Thomas Brennan; shop open every day 9:00-17:00; terms: 'This site is owned and operated by Apeman Interiors, Nunnington Studios, Low Farm, York YO62 5UR'). Shopify store; the products.json feed lists 291 itemised, priced products with photos (Decorative 246, Furniture 35, Lighting 8), e.g. 'Early 19th Century Hongmu Chinese Stool' GBP 950, 'Late 19th Century Chinese Yoke-Ebony (Wumu) Chairs' GBP 750, 'Early 20th Century Indian Brass Chapati Box' GBP 125, 'Early 19th Century Yellow French Confit Pot' GBP 225. Age check on all 291 titles: 232 (80 percent) state a period before 1970 (18th/19th/early 20th century or mid-20th century) and a further 43 are undated antiques, ancient pottery or textiles; the home page says antiques 'predating 1950'. Possible new goods are limited to about 10 textile items (2 titled 'Contemporary' saris and a few kantha quilts and saris), i.e. about 3 percent, below the 5 percent line. No auctions, no contemporary art, no marketplace-only stock; catalogue 291 listings.

omissions: no company name, number or VAT is published; operator recorded as the trading name 'Apeman Interiors' exactly as in the terms of service; the founder Thomas Brennan is named only on the About page, so no legal_name is asserted
logo: the current header logo file is an AI-generated image ('ChatGPT_Image_...png') and the only other brand asset is a GIF, so no logo is asserted

shipping: only free delivery on orders over GBP 35 in England and click-and-collect from the Nunnington shop are recorded; the GBP 10 flat fee for small items under GBP 35, furniture courier surcharges for Highlands, Islands and remote postcodes (quote on request) and 2-6 week furniture lead times are item-class specific or geographically unresolved and are kept out; no foreign destinations stated

decision.basis: AppleMan Antiques (www.applemanshop.com) is an Etsy Pattern storefront: every page carries 'Powered by Etsy', the listing URLs are Etsy listing ids (/listing/4624203781/...), checkout and contact run through Etsy ('Kontaktiere uns auf Etsy') and the terms PDF is hosted on extfiles.etsy.com. The antiques, toys and collectables (priced in EUR converted from GBP) are therefore marketplace-hosted stock only; the operator name, address and e-mail are not shown on the public pages.

Antique Fireplaces London (Shopify; Hertfordshire warehouse; phone 0207 704 0982; 382 itemised priced products in products.json, mostly antique and reclaimed cast-iron, marble and stone fireplace surrounds, inserts, grates and fire baskets, with the stock feed supplied by its sister company The Architectural Forum) also runs a dedicated new-goods part of the shop: a 'British Steel, British made, eco-efficient stoves' collection and a 'Wood Burning & Gas Stoves' menu section (vendor 'London Stove Company', 7 newly manufactured multi-fuel stoves such as 'The Little Thurlow' 5kw DEFRA GBP 1,755), and the home page advertises made-to-measure surrounds. A dedicated new-goods section means NEW_GOODS_MIX under the 2026-11-26 no-mix rule even though it is only about 2 percent of items. The sister site thearchitecturalforum.com is already EXCLUDED NEW_GOODS_MIX in the GB ledger, consistent with this decision.

Antique Baths (Ivybridge, Devon; phone 01752 698250, sales@antiquebaths.com) sells restored original cast-iron roll-top baths from the 1880s-early 1900s (about 25 named baths on the 'Reclaimed Baths' page, prices GBP 1,850-2,895 or TBA) and a restoration service, but the home and shop navigation also carry a dedicated new-goods range: 'Sanitaryware from Silverdale Bathrooms' (newly manufactured Victorian Range ceramics, a current UK manufacturer), 'a small amount of reproduction baths' (home page) and new-build products such as Thomas Crapper & Co prototype washbasins on new oak cabinets. A dedicated new-goods section means NEW_GOODS_MIX under the 2026-11-26 no-mix rule.

Antique Telephones Ltd (company 05947437, Companies House: active private limited company incorporated 2006; site run by Neil Carpenter, phone 020 8290 0539, neilcarpenter38@gmail.com) sells restored original GPO telephones on a ShopFactory shop: about 58 itemised products with photos and prices (GPO 200 series 1929-1959, 300 series 1937-1959, 706 series 1959-1967, 741 wall models, early collectors telephones back to 1904, 746 series 1967-1983 and Trimphones 1966-1984; roughly 60 percent before 1970). Only the registered office is published and the contact page says explicitly it is the accountant's address ('Registered Office Address (Accountant) R Biddle, Mulburry House, Chislehurst'); the trading address of the business is not published anywhere (UK orders posted; collection by prior arrangement only), so no UK trading address can be recorded. Terms also state some items have new parts fitted and several models are re-cased with new mouldings, to be re-read when an address is published.

geography.addressText: Antiques in Oxford, Cumnor Hill, Oxford OX2 9HD, United Kingdom

qualification.basis: Oxfordshire antiques dealer with 40+ years in the trade and ten years online (home page), specialising in silver, jewellery, ceramics, glassware, pewter, buttons and collectables. Wix Stores shop with 1,794 itemised, priced product pages in the store-products sitemap with photos, SKU and Add to Cart (e.g. 'Antique 18ct gold and opal ring' GBP 695, 'Georgian marrow scoop 1790', 'Liberty and Co Archibald Knox silver bowl', 'Early 20th century bi-colour 15ct gold owl brooch' GBP 775), browsable by type and by period (Charles I, Queen Anne, Georgian, William IV, Victorian, Edwardian, George V, Arts and Crafts, Art Nouveau, Art Deco, Vintage). Age check on all 1,794 product slugs: 919 (51 percent) name a period, antique or pre-1950 maker explicitly, 267 more are Danish/Norwegian mid-century silver (Georg Jensen, David-Andersen, Hans Hansen, Evald Nielsen; mostly 1920s-1960s) and 573 are plain items such as antique spoons and pendants; only about 35 slugs (2 percent) are modern or 1970s (Tiffany, Vacheron Constantin, 1970s gold rings), so well over half is pre-1970. Commission sales of clients' items are offered on the same site (accepted as consignment selling). AUCTION SIDE ACTIVITY: the site offers advice on selling on eBay and an auction-agent service that bids for clients at third-party auctions (the shop itself sells at fixed prices; the owner says the eBay shop was closed years ago); no own auctions. Three retail stands (Wallingford, Hungerford, Yarnton antiques centres) sell the same stock. No new goods beyond a few modern designer pieces, no contemporary art, no marketplace-only stock; catalogue about 1,800 listings.

omissions: no company name, number or VAT is published; operator recorded as the trading name; the footer address (Cumnor Hill, Oxford OX2 9HD) is recorded as the business address only, with no showroom claim
logo: the Wix header shows only the site name as text, no own logo image, so no logo is asserted

shipping: the FAQ only says UK buyers pay online by PayPal and overseas buyers must ask for shipping costs first; no destinations, rates or lead times for the shop stock are stated, so no shipping terms are asserted

the three retail stands (Wallingford Antiques Arcade OX10 0AA, Hungerford Arcade Antiques RG17 0NF, Yarnton Antiques Centre OX5 1PA) are third-party centres and are not recorded as locations; platform recorded as WIX from the Wix generator tag, wixstatic assets, Wix store-products sitemap and cart

geography.addressText: 19 East Street, Petworth GU28 0AB, United Kingdom

qualification.basis: Family-run decorative antiques shop at 19 East Street, Petworth, West Sussex (contact page 'Visit US: 19 East Street, Petworth, GU28 0AB'; open Thursday to Tuesday, 'over thirty five years' on the About page). The contact page footer names the operator as 'Antiquities, Arundel Ltd. ( T/A Antiquities Petworth )' and the privacy policy says the site is served by Antiquities, Arundel Ltd.; Companies House lists ANTIQUITIES (ARUNDEL) LIMITED, company 04853127, incorporated 2003 (its registered office in Lancing differs from the shop and is not asserted). Squarespace catalogue by category (furniture, lighting, mirrors, garden and architectural, decorative items, miscellaneous) with about 154 priced items currently available plus sold archives, e.g. 'George II Walnut chest' GBP 3,250, 'Pair of Louis XV giltwood fauteuils' GBP 3,295, 'Regency Rosewood side cabinet Circa 1820' GBP 1,995, 'C19th Burroughs and Watts Snooker Scoreboard' GBP 1,695, 'Early C20th Original painted trade sign' GBP 395. Titles are overwhelmingly C17th-C19th or early C20th, with a few early/mid C20th pieces and some late C20th garden statuary; the page title mentions 'contemporary accessories' but no new goods were seen on the six category pages. No auctions, no contemporary art, no marketplace stock.

omissions: shipping: the site publishes no delivery or collection terms (enquiry-led showroom catalogue), so no shipping terms are asserted
platform recorded as SQUARESPACE from static1.squarespace.com assets and the Squarespace store and gallery URL structure
operator recorded exactly as the footer and privacy policy name it; the Companies House registered office (Lancing) and VAT number are not asserted and the Arundel branch is not a location here

decision.basis: Archaeopteryx Antiquities (Liverpool, 49 Davenham Court L15 8GD, mobile 07739984874, seorasbheag@hotmail.co.uk) is a small dealer in Roman, Romano-British, Saxon and Viking small finds and rings. The site is a brochure: the 'stock-2026' page renders empty in headless Chromium (one placeholder image, no items, no prices) and the home page says the pieces are put on the dealer's Facebook page first and that a 'catalogue card system' is kept there. No itemised stock is inspectable on the dealer's own website.

Antiquary Antiques and Interiors (36 Gloucester St, Malmesbury SN16 0AA; Wix Stores) sells 'antique, vintage and retro' items, but a spread sample of 100 of its shop products (pages 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 of the paginated shop) shows a large new and contemporary share: about 10 titles are new or handmade (e.g. 'Hand Crafted In England A Very Large Metal Peacock Statue', 'Contemporary Indian Mango Wood Cabinet', a hand-made papier-mache tiger sculpture, bespoke painted rocking horse) and at least 9 more are acrylic originals by living artists (Cotswold artist H. Taylour Bay, Paul Westaway, 'A Contemporary Quirky Oil On Canvas Painting'), plus 31 undated 'vintage' items and a new designer glass sculpture, so far above 5 percent of the catalogue is new goods or contemporary art.

Anything In Particular (WooCommerce, 699 itemised products via the store API; shop currently 'taking a break') buys 'items we like' with 'no particular focus or speciality' (About page): toys and games 125, kitsch/weird 122, collectables 190, electricals 57, radios 32, flip clocks 19, everything else 177. Many items are 1970s-1980s nostalgia (e.g. '1980s Saisho PM51P boombox', 'Late 1970s Hitachi digital clock radio', Memphis-style IKEA lamp, 1979 typewriter). Of the 413 listings that carry a year in title or description, only 224 (54 percent) have an earliest year before 1970 and 189 are 1970 or later; the other 286 are undated 'vintage' domestic goods, so a majority before about 1970 cannot be shown. General retro and second-hand collectables, not a specialist antique or vintage dealer.

The Antiques Tourist is a free printed and online South West antiques guide (50,000+ copies a year, 410+ pick-up points; pages: About, FAQs, Previous Editions, Advertise With Us, Contact) that sells advertising to antiques, vintage and reclamation businesses and links to their sites. It is a publisher/directory with no stock of its own; reached as the redirect target of antiquesbazaar.co.uk.

Antiques Reclaimed (family-run antiques and reclamation yard, Atwick Hall Farm, Cliff Road, Atwick YO25 8DF; mobile 07984583383, antiques-reclaimed@hotmail.co.uk; Duda site) lists only 18 priced items on its Store page (e.g. 'Combination Fireplace original with original tiles' GBP 895, 'Victorian Buffet Sideboard' GBP 375, 'Georgian breakfront sideboard' GBP 460, 'Mercers Meat Stout Enamel sign' GBP 325) plus an unlabelled photo gallery of past stock; titles carry no dates and mix Victorian/Georgian pieces with mid-century furniture, a jukebox, industrial lamps and modern collector coins, so a majority before about 1970 cannot be measured with the required confidence from a sample of fewer than 40 dated items. Stock otherwise looks like a genuine antiques and salvage yard with no new goods in the catalogue. Re-check when more itemised, dated stock is published.

Bedford Architectural Antiques (Wix site, 120 Castle Rd, Bedford MK40 3RQ, 01234 213131) is a brochure: the home and 'blank-page' pages describe reclamation and restoration of period fireplaces and doors, a range of new reproduction fireplaces in marble, slate, stone and cast iron, gas fire installation, door stripping and garden items. No itemised stock, photos with item data or prices are published, so there is no inspectable catalogue (and the reproduction fireplaces would be new goods).
The domain serves an Indonesian online-gambling spam page ('Ark Vintage - TOGEL158', AMP version link, logo hot-linked from pdmajugroup.online); no antiques, no business identity, no contact details.

Arthur Lee Interiors (Knutsford, Hollingford House, Toft Road, WA16 0PD; WordPress) is an interiors and paint shop established 1919: Farrow & Ball, Little Greene and Cole & Son paint and wallpaper with in-store tinting machines, a mix of new furniture and interior pieces from suppliers, gift cards. No antiques catalogue, no itemised stock; new-goods retail.

AS Antique Galleries (est. 1973, 26 Broad Street, Pendleton, Salford M6 5BY, open Thu-Sat) deals in genuine Art Nouveau and Art Deco bronzes, lighting, glass and ceramics, but the 2005-era PHP site has no working catalogue: the 'showcase' and 'shop style' pages show only a few thumbnails or 'no style rooms on display', every category page (sculpture, ceramic, furniture) lists the same nine sculpture thumbnails, and every ASItemDetail.php request (checked AS-S01 and AS-S05, also with a cookie jar and referer) returns the same single record (AS-S02, a bronze and ivory pierrette by Paul Phillipe c1930, 'REQUEST PRICE'). Item level stock cannot be inspected reliably; revisit if the catalogue is repaired. The 'auction' flag came only from a PayPal button URL.

Arts Decoratifs (Ann Miller, The Cockpit off Market Hill, Saffron Walden CB10 1HQ; WordPress) is a physical shop presented by a brochure site: home, jewellery, stage/film/TV, gallery and contact pages describe vintage jewellery, glass, ceramics and ephemera in prose and photographs without item titles, prices or an online shop. No itemised stock to inspect; the site also invites sellers to bring jewellery, compacts and fans.

A Box of Frogs (Wragby, Lincolnshire; David Adams and Samantha Shane; WordPress with Elementor) is a 'curio, antique, retro, vintage' shop with local handmade goods. Its home pages 1-3 list about 35 items: Star Wars figures and capes 1977-1983, He-Man Castle Grayskull 1981, Inspector Gadget doll, A-Team van 2001, a Gizmo from Gremlins, a Kartell/Starck Eros chair, a Schwinn Stingray bicycle, uranium glass, a West German vase, Moorcroft and Doulton pieces, a 1937 coronation telephone tray and masonic plates. Pre-1970 items are clearly under half of the listed stock (estimate about one third); nostalgia toys from the 1970s onward and general used goods dominate.

Aspal Antiques is a 3,000 sq ft antiques barn at Stonham Barns, Stowmarket, run as a multi-trader centre: the 'Our Traders' page lists more than a dozen separate traders (Ali's Toy Shed, SF, GP, Southwold Records, JP, LJ, Loumar, LS, RJC, ZBD, Purple Castle, Present Vintage, RPM, PC/PV) selling vinyl records, collectables, costume jewellery, militaria and furniture. The website is a small gallery 'insight' with no itemised or priced stock ('listed items are constantly being sold and withdrawn').

Atburys (WordPress; garage memorabilia, enamel signs, automotive furniture, motorsport limited-edition pictures, Corgi models; trades from pitch 115 of Hungerford Arcade, a multi-dealer antiques centre) shows only a few pictures. Its 'Items for Sale' page just embeds a small selection of listings from the dealer's eBay store ('Buy on eBay': a private number plate, a Schuco Porsche 356, enamel advertising signs) and the site has no own catalogue or cart; limited-edition motorsport prints and advertising signs are largely new or reproduction goods.

Atomic Goose (Abby, 50 Church Street, Donisthorpe DE12 7PY; Wix Stores) shop filters are Antique, Mid Century, Vintage, Kitsch, Boho and 'Eclectic New'; the dedicated 'Eclectic New' section sells newly made decor, and the vintage items are largely 1980s-1990s kitsch (for example a 1980s dead-stock devotional tapestry, a 1990s plush velvet monkey doll couple) next to 1940s-1960s pieces; the about page describes 'blending mid century and vintage influences with contemporary elements'. A vintage/new mix with a dedicated new-goods section.

Attic Antiques (Kirkintilloch, covering Glasgow; Yell.com site, tom.jenkinson48@gmail.com, +44 141 777 7743) is a house-clearance and buying service: 'we will buy furniture, china, clocks, silver, bric-a-brac, old wrist watches, jewellery, medals and coins'. The home, antiques and house-clearance pages offer no stock for sale, no catalogue and no prices.
The domain shows a parked-domain advertising page ('aworldofold.co.uk has expired and may be renewed by the owner', sponsored search topics) with no business, stock or contact.

Bag The Jewels (Caroline Henney Vintage Costume Jewellery, stall at Antiques on High, 85 High Street, Oxford OX1 4BG; ASP shop) sells vintage costume jewellery and bags, but has a dedicated 'New Jewellery' category ('Contemporary Jewellery, Modern Jewellery and New Jewellery': faux turquoise ball earrings and faceted crystal drops on silver ear wires, GBP 10, new Lea Stein brooches). Vintage/new mix with a dedicated new-goods section.

Bargain Centre (Paisley Shopping Centre unit, 07445 867027; Ueni one-page site) is a thrift and consignment store for old clothing, household appliances, electrical items and pet supplies; antiques are mentioned only as consignment items. No catalogue and no qualified antique stock.

Barley Sugar (1 Cornfield Terrace, Eastbourne BN21 4NN, 01323 729577) is an artisan delicatessen, wine merchant and lifestyle store with contemporary homeware; the 'Vintage Finds' page offers antiques used to prop the shop in a text paragraph only, with no itemised stock. New food, wine and homeware retail without an antiques catalogue.

Bedsteads (Chelvey Court Barn near Bristol, 01275 464114) sells antique and lightly restored beds but its navigation also holds dedicated 'reproduction beds' (Reproduction, Edwardian, Victorian, Replica beds) and 'mattresses & bases' sections, and the text says the team 'recreates' antique beds. Vintage/new mix with dedicated new-goods sections.

Beech And Springs (WordPress) is an upholstery, French polishing and furniture restoration service. Its 'Antiques Store' menu entry leads to the dealer's storefront 'Beech and Springs Antiques' (Kent, 97 items) on the Sellingantiques.co.uk marketplace; the own domain has no catalogue of stock, so the stock is marketplace-only.

Berridges Jewellers (4 Dial Lane, Ipswich IP1 1DL; WordPress/WooCommerce; jeweller since 1994 with a restaurant upstairs). The separate online Vintage Shop (secure.berridges.com/shop, WooCommerce Store API, 325 itemised priced pieces: Victorian 116, Edwardian 78, Art Deco 49, Art Nouveau 7, Retro 12, 'Pre Owned' 63; clearly about 75-80 percent pre-1970) would qualify on stock alone. But the operator's own website presents a new-goods jewellery business next to it: the Collections page lists Chimento, Georg Jensen, Richard Hans Becker, Thomas Sabo and new diamond, engagement and wedding rings, plus a restaurant and a 'Contemporary Jewellery' menu entry in the vintage shop. Policy of 2026-11-26 (no vintage/new mix, dedicated new-goods shop part) applies; the vintage catalogue is a candidate for an owner override if only that catalogue should count.

Berry Vintage (WordPress/WooCommerce) sells 'vintage' and pre-owned jewellery; the Store API lists 35 products of which only two carry a pre-1970 date (Vintage (1940) 18ct band, Vintage (1967) 18ct diamond ring) while most are 'pre owned' modern gold jewellery or 1970s-1990s pieces (Vintage 1990, 1993, 1976, 1978, 1980s Monet and Givenchy costume jewellery). Share of pre-1970 stock about 6 percent.

The site answers HTTP 200 with a hosting notice: 'This website has been suspended and is no longer available. If you are the website owner, please contact us to restore your website.' No dealer content is visible, so current activity cannot be established; recheck later.

Atelier Kingsley (Wix Stores, 196 product URLs in the store sitemap, mostly sold-archive items at GBP 0; MID-CENTURY DESIGN and ECLECTIC VINTAGE DECOR) publishes only info@atelierkingsley.com: the about, contact and shipping pages 404 (help page and policy pages checked), the privacy and terms pages name no operator, address or phone, and 'Worldwide Delivery' is the only logistics text. No UK trading address or operator can be asserted. The antique share is also unconfirmed: dated slugs give about 57 pre-1970 against 14 from the 1970s on, but 125 items are undated (Murano glass, Gallotti & Radice, B&B Italia, 'in the style of' pieces, studio glass and 1970s graphite drawings), so the majority-pre-1970 rule is not proven.

Bellemoon Vintage and Welsh Blankets (Tracey Stedman; Shopify; physical shop in Abergavenny Market Hall NP7 5EH open Tuesday and Saturday; Welsh blankets, vintage jewellery, china, kitchenalia, home decor, items such as Art Deco barbola mirrors and 1930s brooches) publishes no email address and no phone number: the contact page is a form only, and the shipping policy ('Royal Mail tracked, UK mainland only') carries no contact either. Cannot be onboarded without a published contact.

Barographs For Sale (Wix Stores, about 250 product URLs: barographs, thermographs, barometers by Negretti & Zambra and others, mostly Victorian to 1950s, prices GBP 325-825 visible, e.g. 1930s station barograph) is the sale of 'a unique 60 year collection' by Richard Twort (Weston-super-Mare, Somerset; rtwort@hotmail.com, +44 7711 939 789) who says he needs to 'slim down my collection'; the instruments 'are now held locally in secure storage', payment and delivery are arranged by contact after a cart request, and no business name, company or street address is published. decision.basis: Chart Sutton Antiques Centre (IONOS MyWebsite, Pleasant View Garden Centre, Chart Sutton near Maidstone, Kent) is a multi-dealer antiques centre: the Our Dealers page says 'over 20 dealers selling within the centre' on cabinets and pitches with waiting lists for new dealers. The 'Online shop window' pages show only 'a very small selection' of the centre's mixed stock by category and state 'We do not currently sell online'; items may be sold or held by rotating dealers. No single dealer owns the stock and there is no itemised, purchasable catalogue of one operator.

Chelmsford Militaria (WooCommerce, about 950 products in the public store API, 1,700 items claimed on the home page) sells deactivated firearms, bayonets, inert ammunition, magazines, pouches and accessories, an estimated 55 per cent of them with titles that point to WW1/WW2 or earlier originals. But the catalogue carries a dedicated 'REPLICA AND FILM PROPS' category (23 items, for example Denix non-firing replicas of the Sten Mk2, MP40, Garand, Luger and AK47 at GBP 105-235, and film props made for the film Fury) plus other new-made goods (Manroy-made M4 magazine, Magpul hand guard and E-mag, 'M1 Carbine repro pouch kit'), and a further estimated 14 per cent of titles are clearly post-1970 (AK74, Galil, SA80, Steyr AUG/MP9, Type 85, baton and 5.56 drill rounds) with about 29 per cent undatable. A dedicated new-goods section and a majority that cannot be shown to be pre-1970 rule it out under the no-vintage/new-mix rule. No auctions seen.

Cheshire Vintage Furniture (Hale, Altrincham; WordPress with an IONOS/Ecwid store, free collection and a fixed GBP 30 delivery within 10 miles) is a general second-hand 'affordable vintage, antique and unique furniture' shop with a full house-clearance service and 'many more, smaller items in store, not on the website'. A rendered read of the shop categories (Seating 14 items, Sideboards/Shelving/Cabinets/Desks 32 items, Reduced to clear, Garden Furniture and others) shows mostly undated everyday used furniture (tan leather chesterfield, 'Next Sherlock wingback chair', rustic coffee table, Ercol Renaissance suite, large garden gazebo, 'small french style drawers' at 40 per cent off); of 26 titles read only about 7 could be placed before 1970 (19th century Windsor chair, antique prie-dieu, G Plan Housemaster chairs, Robert Heritage and teak mid-century sideboards, Victorian breakfront sideboard). The site also has a dedicated 'Christmas Trees' page for Nordmann trees. The catalogue is not predominantly antique or vintage (made before about 1970).

Clockprops (Roger Lascelles, Wix store, 34 products in the store sitemap, London SW17 showroom by appointment) sells and hires vintage and antique clocks, but a large share of the catalogue is newly made decorative stock: product pages describe clocks 'we have made in the old style' (248 Large Traditional Wall Clock, a metal dial on an old French wine barrel with modern quartz, GBP 550), a new 'distressed' turret dial (574 Yellow Turret Clock), '691 Large French style turret clock (new)' made from an antique barrel lid, and '084 Antique Clock Dial in Boxed Frame' (an old dial in a newly made pastel case). The shop also has 'Bespoke' and 'Gift Ideas' sections, Balinese paintings and a 'Made in England' Lascelles wall clock, and many old clocks are fitted with new quartz movements. Of 16 product pages read, 4 are new-made pieces (25 per cent), far beyond the 5 per cent tolerance.

Coco Collectables (Wix store, UK delivery only) sells 'mid to late 20th century' art glass, ceramics, kitchenalia, barware and jewellery; the About and header text describe 'mid-century, vintage, retro & funky collectables: 1960s-1980s' (West German pottery, fat lava, Rosenthal Studio-Line, Murano ashtrays, Guzzini lucite). Of the 12 items on the shop home page, 3 carry an explicit 1970s date (Team Guzzini giraffe, Rosenthal Baumann vase, Murano bowl), one is dated 1960 (Czech Rosice vase) and the rest are undated retro, op-art, space-age or fat-lava pieces of the 1960s-70s. The stock is 1970s-80s nostalgia, not predominantly before about 1970. No postal address is published either (only 'live in Sussex' and an email).

Coles Antiques and Jewellery (Wix, 9 Boulevard, Weston-super-Mare BS23 1NN; Matthew, Natalie and Aaron Coles) is a family shop and house-clearance firm (licensed waste carrier) selling antique furniture, gold, silver and jewellery from the showroom. The website has no catalogue: the Jewellery page is a short photo gallery (a handful of entries such as '9ct Gold Horse Head Stick Pin' and 'Vintage Ladies Gold Mechanical Watch, Chester 1932') with no prices, no item pages and no way to buy, and the Stock/Contact page directs buyers to the showroom, Etsy (ColesJewellery) and LoveAntiques. No itemised, priced online stock of identifiable antiques exists on the site.

Country House Fine Art (Shopify, 116 products in the public collection, free UK mainland delivery, worldwide on quote) sells 17th to 19th century portraits and landscapes, silver and a few antiques, and would otherwise qualify. But a dedicated 'limited edition prints' collection holds 10 in-stock products (8.6 per cent of the catalogue) of new prints by living or recently active artists (for example Fabian Perez, Alexander Millar and Beryl Cook limited editions at GBP 495-995), above the 5 per cent tolerance for new goods. In addition no postal address is published (contact page: form, sales@countryhousefineart.co.uk and two phone numbers; 'now selling solely online'). No auctions seen.

Joes MCM (SumUp online store; sells at fairs such as St Ives Antiques Fair) offers 'vintage & retro glass, ceramics, jewellery' together with new work by living studio-glass artists. In the studio-glass page at least 8 of 16 items are current pieces by living British makers (five Thomas Petit pieces, one 'signed and dated 2026', two Jane Charles sculptures, Norman Stuart Clarke), the new-stock page offers a Lalique Splash dolphin 'produced in 2006', Clogau and Patrick Mavros jewellery, and the category list names living or modern makers (Peter Layton, Graeme Hawes, Okra, Station Glass, Mdina, Langham, Isle of Wight Glass) with most rings and glass dated 1970s to 2026 (rings dated 1975, 1980, 1981, 1996). New goods far exceed 5 per cent and the stock is not predominantly pre-1970. No postal address is published on the contact page either.

Meanwhile, all stock can be viewed at SellingAntiques'. The only inspectable catalogue (143 items, antique furniture and decorative pieces) is the dealer's storefront on the sellingantiques.co.uk marketplace (sellingantiques.co.uk/jdrake), not an own site, so the stock is marketplace-only.
